title.zh: 卷三百二十七 列傳第二百十五 外國八 韃靼
title.raw: 卷三百二十七 列傳第二百十五 外國八 韃靼 Volume 327 Biographies 215: Foreign States 8

sentences.zh: 韃靼，即蒙古，故元後也。

translations.literal: The Tartars are the Mongols, the successors of the former Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartars are the Mongols—the remnant house of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖洪武元年，大將軍徐達率師取元，元主自北平遁出塞，居開平，數遣其將也速等擾北邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu under the founding emperor, Grand General Xu Da led troops to take the Yuan; the Yuan ruler fled from Beiping out beyond the passes, dwelt at Kaiping, and repeatedly sent his generals Yisu and others to harass the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding emperor’s first Hongwu year, Grand General Xu Da marched to seize the Yuan capital; the Yuan emperor slipped from Beiping north of the passes and made Kaiping his seat, while repeatedly dispatching generals such as Yisu to raid the northern border.

sentences.zh: 明年，常遇春擊敗之，師進開平，俘宗王慶孫、平章鼎住。

translations.literal: The next year Chang Yuchun defeated them; the army advanced to Kaiping and captured the imperial prince Qing Sun and the chancellor Dingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chang Yuchun routed them; the army pushed on to Kaiping and took the imperial prince Qing Sun and Chancellor Dingzhu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 時元主奔應昌，其將王保保據定西為邊患。

translations.literal: At this time the Yuan ruler fled to Yingchang; his general Wang Baobao held Dingxi and became a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yuan emperor had fled to Yingchang, while his general Wang Baobao held Dingxi and plagued the border.

sentences.zh: 三年春，以徐達為大將軍，使出西安搗定西；

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Xu Da was made grand general and ordered to march out from Xi’an to strike Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Xu Da was appointed grand general and directed to advance from Xi’an against Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 李文忠為左副將軍，馮勝為右副將軍，使出居庸搗應昌。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong was made left vice grand general and Feng Sheng right vice grand general, ordered to march out through Juyong to strike Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong and Feng Sheng were named left and right vice grand generals, ordered out through Juyong Pass to strike Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 文忠至興和，擒平章竹貞，復大破元兵於駱駝山，遂趨應昌。

translations.literal: Wenzhong reached Xinghe, captured the chancellor Zhuzhen, again routed Yuan troops at Camel Mountain, and then hurried toward Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong reached Xinghe, seized Chancellor Zhuzhen, won another great victory over Yuan forces at Camel Mountain, and pressed on toward Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 未至，知元主已殂，進圍其城，克之。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he learned the Yuan ruler had died; he advanced to besiege its city and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he learned the Yuan emperor was already dead; he advanced, laid siege to the city, and took it.

sentences.zh: 獲元主孫買的裡八剌及其妃嬪、大臣、寶玉、圖籍。

translations.literal: He captured the Yuan ruler’s grandson Maidibaer and his consorts, great ministers, precious jades, and registers.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Yuan emperor’s grandson Maidibaer along with the imperial women, high ministers, jewels, and court registers.

sentences.zh: 太子愛猷識理達臘獨以數十騎遁去。

translations.literal: The crown prince Ayushiridara alone fled away with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ayushiridara alone escaped with a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 而徐達亦大破王保保兵於沈兒峪口，走之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xu Da also greatly defeated Wang Baobao’s troops at Shen’er Valley Pass and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Da routed Wang Baobao’s army at Shen’er Valley Pass and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 太祖封買的裡八剌為崇禮侯，謚元主曰順帝。

translations.literal: The founding emperor enfeoffed Maidibaer as Marquis Chongli and gave the Yuan ruler the posthumous title Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor enfeoffed Maidibaer as Marquis Chongli and posthumously styled the Yuan emperor as Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 於是故元諸將江文清等、王子失篤兒等，先後歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon former Yuan generals such as Jiang Wenqing and princes such as Shiduer successively submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter former Yuan commanders such as Jiang Wenqing and princes such as Shiduer submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 獨王保保擁太子愛猷識理達臘居和林，屢詔諭之，不從。

translations.literal: Only Wang Baobao, holding Crown Prince Ayushiridara, dwelt at Karakorum; edicts repeatedly instructed him, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Baobao, keeping Crown Prince Ayushiridara with him at Karakorum, defied repeated imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 五年春，命大將軍徐達、左副將軍李文忠、征西將軍馮勝率師三道征之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he ordered Grand General Xu Da, Left Vice Grand General Li Wenzhong, and Western Campaign General Feng Sheng to lead armies in three columns to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he ordered Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, and Western Campaign General Feng Sheng to take the field in three columns against them.

sentences.zh: 大將軍達由中路出雁門，戰不利，守塞。

translations.literal: Grand General Da marched by the central route out through Yanmen; the battle went badly and he held the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da took the central route through Yanmen Pass; the fighting went poorly and he fell back to hold the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 勝軍西次蘭州。

translations.literal: Sheng’s army halted in the west at Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng’s column encamped in the west at Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 右副將軍傅友德先進，轉戰至埽林山，勝等兵合，斬其平章不花，降上都驢等所部吏民八千三百餘戶，遂由亦集乃路至瓜、沙州，復連敗之。

translations.literal: Right Vice Grand General Fu Youde advanced first, fought through to Saolin Mountain; Sheng and the others united their forces, beheaded their chancellor Buhua, and received the surrender of more than eight thousand three hundred households of officials and people under Shangdu Lü and others; then by way of Ejinay to Guazhou and Shazhou they again defeated them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Grand General Fu Youde pushed ahead, fighting his way to Saolin Mountain; when Feng Sheng’s forces joined him they slew the Yuan chancellor Buhua and accepted the surrender of more than eight thousand three hundred households under Shangdu Lü and his followers; then marching by Ejinay to Guazhou and Shazhou they inflicted defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 文忠東出居庸至口溫，元將棄營遁，乃率輕騎自臚朐河疾馳，進敗蠻子哈剌章於土剌河，追及阿魯渾河，又追及稱海，獲其官屬子孫並軍士家屬千八百餘，送京師。

translations.literal: Wenzhong marched east out through Juyong to Kouwen; Yuan generals abandoned their camps and fled; he then led light cavalry in a swift ride from the Luqu River, advanced and defeated Manzi Hala Zhang at the Tula River, pursued to the Arun River, and pursued again to Changhai, capturing more than eighteen hundred officials, dependents, and soldiers’ families and sending them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong marched east through Juyong to Kouwen; when Yuan commanders abandoned camp and fled he led light horse in a dash from the Luqu River, defeated Manzi Hala Zhang on the Tula, pursued him to the Arun and then to Changhai, and sent more than eighteen hundred officials, kin, and soldiers’ families to the capital as captives.

sentences.zh: 達等尋召還。

translations.literal: Da and the others were soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and the other columns were soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣達、文忠等備西北邊。

translations.literal: The next spring he dispatched Da, Wenzhong, and others to guard the northwest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he sent Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, and others to secure the northwest frontier.

sentences.zh: 元兵入犯武、朔，達遣陳德、郭子興擊破之。

translations.literal: Yuan troops invaded Wu and Shuo; Da sent Chen De and Guo Zixing to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces raided Wu and Shuo, Xu Da sent Chen De and Guo Zixing to rout them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，達等復大破王保保兵於懷柔。

translations.literal: Before long Da and the others again greatly defeated Wang Baobao’s troops at Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xu Da again inflicted a major defeat on Wang Baobao’s army at Huairou.

sentences.zh: 時元兵先後犯白登、保德、河曲，輒為守將所敗，獨撫寧、瑞州被殘，太祖乃徙其民於內地。

translations.literal: At this time Yuan troops successively invaded Baideng, Baode, and Hequ and were each time defeated by defending generals; only Funing and Ruizhou were ravaged, whereupon the founding emperor relocated their people to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan raids on Baideng, Baode, and Hequ were beaten back by local defenders, but Funing and Ruizhou suffered devastation, so the founding emperor resettled their populations inland.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，都督藍玉拔興和。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year Regional Commander Lan Yu captured Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year Regional Commander Lan Yu took Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 文忠亦遣裨將擒斬其長，而自以大軍攻高州大石崖，克之，斬宗王、大臣朵朵失裡等，至氈帽山斬魯王，獲其妃蒙哥禿。

translations.literal: Wenzhong also sent a subordinate general to capture and behead their chief, while he himself with the main army attacked the great stone cliffs of Gaozhou, captured them, and beheaded the imperial prince and great minister Duoduoshili and others; reaching Zhanmao Mountain he beheaded the Prince of Lu and captured his consort Menggutu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong sent a lieutenant to capture and behead a tribal chief, while he led the main force against the great cliffs of Gaozhou, took them, and slew the imperial prince and minister Duoduoshili; at Zhanmao Mountain he killed the Prince of Lu and took his consort Menggutu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 秋，太祖以故元太子流離沙漠，父子隔絕，未有後嗣，乃遣崇禮侯北歸，以書諭之。

translations.literal: In autumn, because the former Yuan crown prince was adrift in the desert, father and son separated and without heirs, the founding emperor sent the Marquis Chongli north to return home with a letter instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, moved that the former Yuan crown prince wandered the desert cut off from his father and without heirs, the founding emperor sent Marquis Chongli north with a letter of counsel.

sentences.zh: 又二年，其部下九住等寇西邊，敗去。

translations.literal: Two years later his subordinates Jiuzhu and others raided the western frontier and were defeated and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later his followers Jiuzhu and others raided the western border and were beaten off.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年夏，故元太子愛猷識理達臘卒，太祖自為文，遣使弔祭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year of Hongwu the former Yuan crown prince Ayushiridara died; the founding emperor himself composed the text and sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Hongwu eleven the former Yuan crown prince Ayushiridara died; the founding emperor wrote the mourning text himself and sent envoys to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 子脫古思帖木兒繼立。

translations.literal: His son Togus Temür succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Togus Temür succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其丞相驢兒、蠻子哈剌章，國公脫火赤，平章完者不花、乃兒不花，樞密知院愛足等，擁眾於應昌、和林，時出沒塞下。

translations.literal: His chancellor Lü’er, Manzi Hala Zhang, the state duke Tuohuochi, the chancellors Wanzhubuhua and Naierbuhua, and the privy councilor Aizu and others held their followers at Yingchang and Karakorum and from time to time appeared and vanished below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Lü’er, Manzi Hala Zhang, State Duke Tuohuochi, chancellors Wanzhubuhua and Naierbuhua, and Privy Councilor Aizu held forces at Yingchang and Karakorum, raiding below the passes whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 太祖屢賜璽書諭之，不從。

translations.literal: The founding emperor repeatedly bestowed sealed edicts instructing them, but they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent repeated sealed edicts, but they would not submit.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，西平侯沐英師出靈州，渡黃河，歷賀蘭山，踐流沙，擒脫火赤、愛足等於和林，盡以其部曲歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying’s army marched out from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River, passed Helan Mountain, trod the drifting sands, and at Karakorum captured Tuohuochi, Aizu, and others, bringing all their followers back in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying marched from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River, crossed Helan Mountain and the drifting sands, and at Karakorum captured Tuohuochi, Aizu, and others with all their followers.

sentences.zh: 冬，完者不花亦就擒。

translations.literal: In winter Wanzhubuhua was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wanzhubuhua was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 明年春，徐達及副將軍湯和、傅友德征乃兒不花，至河北，襲灰山，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The next spring Xu Da with Vice Generals Tang He and Fu Youde campaigned against Naierbuhua, reached Hebei, raided Huishan, and slew and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Xu Da with Tang He and Fu Youde campaigned against Naierbuhua, reached Hebei, struck Huishan, and took a great toll in heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 時王保保已先卒，諸巨魁多以次平定，或望風歸附，獨丞相納哈出擁二十萬眾據金山，數窺伺遼。

translations.literal: By then Wang Baobao had already died; most of the great chieftains were pacified in turn or submitted at the first rumor of force; only Chancellor Naghachu held two hundred thousand men on Jinshan and repeatedly watched for an opportunity against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Baobao was already dead; most of the great leaders had been subdued or had submitted at a rumor of arms—only Chancellor Naghachu, with two hundred thousand men on Jinshan, kept probing Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，命宋國公馮勝為大將軍，率潁川侯傅友德、永昌侯藍玉等，將兵二十萬征之，還其先所獲元將乃剌吾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he ordered Duke of Song Feng Sheng as grand general, leading Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde, Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu, and others with two hundred thousand troops to campaign against him, and returned the formerly captured Yuan general Nairuwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year he appointed Duke of Song Feng Sheng grand general, with Fu Youde, Lan Yu, and others leading two hundred thousand men against Naghachu, and sent back the captured Yuan general Nairuwu.

sentences.zh: 勝軍駐通州，遣藍玉乘大雪襲慶州，克之。

translations.literal: Sheng’s army encamped at Tongzhou and sent Lan Yu to strike Qingzhou amid heavy snow; he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng encamped at Tongzhou and sent Lan Yu to storm Qingzhou in a blizzard; the city fell.

sentences.zh: 夏，師逾金山，臨江侯陳鏞失道，陷敵死。

translations.literal: In summer the army crossed Jinshan; Marquis of Linjiang Chen Yong lost his way, fell into the enemy, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the army crossed Jinshan; Marquis of Linjiang Chen Yong lost his way, was trapped by the enemy, and killed.

sentences.zh: 乃剌吾歸，備以朝廷撫卹恩語其眾，於是全國公觀童來降。

translations.literal: Nairuwu returned and fully recounted to his followers the court’s grace in soothing and succoring them; thereupon the state duke Guantong came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Nairuwu returned and told his followers at length of the court’s kindness; then State Duke Guantong submitted.

sentences.zh: 納哈出因聞乃剌吾之言已心悸，復為大軍所迫，乃陽使人至大將軍營納款，以覘兵勢。

translations.literal: Naghachu, having heard Nairuwu’s words, was already fearful at heart; pressed again by the great army, he feigned sending men to the grand general’s camp to offer submission in order to spy on the army’s strength.
translations.idiomatic: Naghachu was already shaken by Nairuwu’s report and, pressed by the main army, sent envoys under the guise of surrender to scout Ming strength.

sentences.zh: 勝遣玉往受降。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Yu to receive the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng sent Lan Yu to accept the surrender.

sentences.zh: 使者見勝軍還報，納哈出仰天嘆曰：「天弗使吾有此眾矣。」

translations.literal: The envoys saw Sheng’s army and returned to report; Naghachu looked up to heaven and sighed, saying: “Heaven will not let me keep this host.”
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys saw Feng Sheng’s host and reported back, Naghachu looked to heaven and sighed: “Heaven will not let me keep this host.”

sentences.zh: 遂率數百騎詣玉納降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several hundred horsemen to go to Yu and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then led several hundred riders to Lan Yu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 已，將脫去，為鄭國公常茂所傷不得去。

translations.literal: Presently, about to slip away, he was wounded by Duke of Zheng Chang Mao and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to slip away, Duke of Zheng Chang Mao wounded him and he could not escape.

sentences.zh: 都督耿忠遂以眾擁之見勝，勝重禮之，使忠與同寢食。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Geng Zhong then with his troops escorted him to see Sheng; Sheng treated him with great courtesy and had Zhong share bed and board with him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Geng Zhong escorted him with troops to Feng Sheng, who honored him richly and had Zhong share quarters and meals with him.

sentences.zh: 先後降其部曲二十餘萬人，及聞納哈出傷，由是驚潰者四萬人，獲輜重畜馬亙百餘里。

translations.literal: In succession more than two hundred thousand of his followers submitted; when they heard Naghachu was wounded, forty thousand more fled in panic; baggage, livestock, and horses captured stretched for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand of his followers surrendered in succession; when word spread that Naghachu was wounded, another forty thousand broke in panic; captured baggage and herds stretched for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 勝班師，都督濮英以三千騎殿，為潰卒所邀襲，死之。

translations.literal: Sheng withdrew the army; Regional Commander Pu Ying with three thousand horsemen brought up the rear and was ambushed by fleeing soldiers and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng withdrew; Regional Commander Pu Ying with three thousand horse covered the retreat and was ambushed and killed by fleeing troops.

sentences.zh: 秋，勝等表上納哈出所部官屬二百餘人，將校三千三百餘人，金銀銅印一百顆，虎符牌面百二十五事，馬二百九十餘匹， 稱賀。

translations.literal: In autumn Sheng and the others memorialized presenting more than two hundred officials of Naghachu’s following, more than three thousand three hundred officers, one hundred gold, silver, and bronze seals, one hundred twenty-five tiger tallies and plaques, and more than two hundred ninety horses, offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Feng Sheng memorialized the surrender of more than two hundred of Naghachu’s officials, more than three thousand three hundred officers, one hundred gold, silver, and bronze seals, one hundred twenty-five tiger tallies and plaques, and nearly three hundred horses, with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太祖封納哈出為海西侯，先後賜予甚厚，並授乃剌吾千戶。

translations.literal: The founding emperor enfeoffed Naghachu as Marquis of Haixi, bestowed gifts on him very generously before and after, and also appointed Nairuwu a chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor enfeoffed Naghachu as Marquis of Haixi, lavished gifts upon him, and appointed Nairuwu a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 納哈出既降，帝以故元遺寇終為邊患，乃即軍中拜藍玉為大將軍，唐勝、郭英副之，耿忠、孫恪為左、右參將，率師十五萬往征之。

translations.literal: After Naghachu had submitted, the emperor, because remnant Yuan raiders would ultimately be a frontier trouble, then and there in the army appointed Lan Yu grand general, with Tang Sheng and Guo Ying as his deputies and Geng Zhong and Sun Ke as left and right staff generals, leading one hundred fifty thousand troops to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Naghachu had surrendered, the emperor, fearing remnant Yuan bands would plague the border, appointed Lan Yu grand general on the spot, with Tang Sheng and Guo Ying as deputies and Geng Zhong and Sun Ke as staff generals, and sent one hundred fifty thousand men against them.

sentences.zh: 冬，元將脫脫等降於玉。

translations.literal: In winter Yuan generals Toto and others submitted to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yuan generals Toto and others surrendered to Lan Yu.

sentences.zh: 明年春，玉以大軍由大寧至慶州，聞脫古思帖木兒在捕魚兒海，從間道馳進，至百眼井哨不見敵，欲引還。

translations.literal: The next spring Yu with the great army went from Daining to Qingzhou; hearing Togus Temür was at Buir Lake, he hurried by a bypath; reaching the Baiyanjing outpost he saw no enemy and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Lan Yu marched from Daining to Qingzhou; learning Togus Temür was at Buir Lake he took a hidden route in haste; at the Baiyanjing outpost he found no enemy and meant to turn back.

sentences.zh: 定遠侯王弼曰：「吾等奉聖主威德，提十萬餘眾，深入至此，無所得，何以覆命？」

translations.literal: Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi said: “We have received the sacred ruler’s majesty and virtue, leading more than one hundred thousand men deep to this place—if we gain nothing, how can we answer for our mission?”
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi said: “We march under the Son of Heaven’s majesty with more than one hundred thousand men this deep into the steppe—if we return empty-handed, how do we answer for it?”

sentences.zh: 玉乃穴地而爨，一夜馳至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: Yu then dug pits in the ground to cook and in one night galloped to Buir Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yu dug fire pits in the earth and in one night galloped to Buir Lake.

sentences.zh: 黎明，去敵營八十里。

translations.literal: At dawn they were eighty li from the enemy camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they were eighty li from the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 時大風揚沙，晝晦，軍行無知者，敵不設備。

translations.literal: At this time a great wind raised sand; day was dim; the army marched without being detected; the enemy made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: A sandstorm darkened the day; the army advanced undetected while the enemy stood unprepared.

sentences.zh: 弼為前鋒，直薄之，遂大破其軍，斬太尉、蠻子數千人。

translations.literal: Bi served as vanguard and pressed straight upon them; he then routed their army greatly and beheaded several thousand grand marshals and Manzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi led the van in a direct assault and shattered their army, slaying several thousand grand marshals and Manzi.

sentences.zh: 脫古思帖木兒以其太子天保奴、知院捏怯來、丞相失烈門等數十騎遁去，獲其次子地保奴及妃主五十餘人、渠率三千、男女七萬餘，馬駝牛羊十萬，聚鎧仗焚之。

translations.literal: Togus Temür with his crown prince Tianbaonu, the privy councilor Nieqielai, Chancellor Shiliemen, and several dozen horsemen fled; they captured his second son Dibaonu and more than fifty consorts and princesses, three thousand chieftains, more than seventy thousand men and women, one hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep; they heaped armor and weapons and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Togus Temür fled with Crown Prince Tianbaonu, Privy Councilor Nieqielai, Chancellor Shiliemen, and a few dozen riders; they took his second son Dibaonu, more than fifty imperial women, three thousand chiefs, more than seventy thousand people, and one hundred thousand head of livestock, then heaped and burned the captured arms.

sentences.zh: 又破其將哈剌章營，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: They again broke the camp of his general Hala Zhang and wholly received the submission of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: They then overran General Hala Zhang’s camp and accepted the surrender of all his followers.

sentences.zh: 於是漠北削平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the northern desert was leveled.
translations.idiomatic: The northern steppe was thus pacified.

sentences.zh: 捷奏至，太祖大悅，賜地保奴等鈔幣，命有司給供具。

translations.literal: When the victory memorial arrived the founding emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed paper money on Dibaonu and others, and ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victory arrived the founding emperor was delighted, gave Dibaonu and the others paper money, and ordered the ministries to provide for them.

sentences.zh: 既有言玉私元主妃者，帝怒，妃慚懼自殺。

translations.literal: When there were reports that Yu had privately taken a Yuan imperial consort, the emperor was angry; the consort, ashamed and afraid, killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Lan Yu had taken a Yuan imperial consort, the emperor was furious; the woman, ashamed and afraid, took her own life.

sentences.zh: 地保奴出怨言，帝居之琉球。

translations.literal: Dibaonu uttered resentful words; the emperor settled him in Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dibaonu spoke bitterly; the emperor sent him to live in Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 脫古思帖木兒既遁，將依丞相咬住於和林，行至土剌河，為其下也速迭兒所襲，眾復散，獨與捏怯來等十六騎偕。

translations.literal: After Togus Temür had fled he was about to rely on Chancellor Yaoqiao at Karakorum; reaching the Tula River he was attacked by his subordinate Yisu Tiejier; his followers scattered again; he was left with only Nieqielai and sixteen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Togus Temür fled toward Chancellor Yaoqiao at Karakorum; on the Tula River his follower Yisu Tiejier attacked him, his band scattered again, and only Nieqielai and sixteen riders remained.

sentences.zh: 適咬住來迎，欲共往依闊闊帖木兒，大雪不得發。

translations.literal: Just then Yaoqiao came to meet him; they wished to go together to rely on Kuokuotiemuer, but heavy snow prevented them from setting out.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqiao came to meet him; they planned to join Kuokuotiemuer, but heavy snow kept them from moving.

sentences.zh: 也速迭兒兵猝至，縊殺之，並殺天保奴。

translations.literal: Yisu Tiejier’s troops suddenly arrived, strangled him to death, and also killed Tianbaonu.
translations.idiomatic: Yisu Tiejier’s men struck suddenly, strangled Togus Temür, and killed Tianbaonu as well.

sentences.zh: 於是捏怯來、失烈門等來降，置之全寧衛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nieqielai, Shiliemen, and others came to submit and were placed in Quanning Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Nieqielai, Shiliemen, and others then submitted and were settled in Quanning Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，捏怯來為失烈門所襲殺，眾潰，詔朵顏等衛招撫之，來降者益眾。

translations.literal: Before long Nieqielai was attacked and killed by Shiliemen; the masses scattered; an edict ordered the Duoyan and other guards to win them over, and those who came to submit grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shiliemen attacked and killed Nieqielai; the bands scattered; an edict ordered the Duoyan guards and others to win them over, and submissions increased.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，命潁國公傅友德等以北平兵從燕王，定遠侯王弼等以山西兵從晉王，征咬住及乃兒不花、阿魯帖木兒等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year he ordered Duke of Ying Fu Youde and others with Beiping troops to follow the Prince of Yan, and Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi and others with Shanxi troops to follow the Prince of Jin, to campaign against Yaoqiao, Naierbuhua, Alutiemuer, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year he ordered Duke of Ying Fu Youde with Beiping troops under the Prince of Yan and Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi with Shanxi troops under the Prince of Jin against Yaoqiao, Naierbuhua, Alutiemuer, and others.

sentences.zh: 燕王出古北口，偵知乃兒不花營迤都，冒大雪馳進，去敵一磧，敵不知也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan marched out through Gubeikou, reconnoitered and learned Naierbuhua’s camp was at Yidu, dashed forward through heavy snow, and was one desert stretch from the enemy, who did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan marched through Gubeikou, learned Naierbuhua was encamped at Yidu, and galloped through a blizzard to within one desert march—undetected.

sentences.zh: 先遣指揮觀童往，觀童舊與乃兒不花善，一見相持泣。

translations.literal: He first sent Commander Guan Tong ahead; Guan Tong had long been on good terms with Naierbuhua; at first sight they embraced each other weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Commander Guan Tong, an old friend of Naierbuhua’s; at sight they embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 頃之，大軍壓其營，乃兒不花驚，欲遁，觀童止之，引見王，賜飲食慰諭遣還。

translations.literal: Shortly the great army pressed on his camp; Naierbuhua was alarmed and wished to flee; Guan Tong stopped him, led him to see the prince, who bestowed food and drink, comforted and instructed him, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main army closed on the camp; Naierbuhua panicked and tried to flee; Guan Tong restrained him, brought him before the prince, who fed him, reassured him, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 乃兒不花喜過望，遂偕咬住等來降。

translations.literal: Naierbuhua was happier than he had hoped; he then came to submit together with Yaoqiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Naierbuhua was overjoyed and came to submit with Yaoqiao and the others.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃兒不花等以謀叛誅死，敵益衰。

translations.literal: After a long time Naierbuhua and others were executed for plotting rebellion, and the enemy grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: In time Naierbuhua and others were executed for plotting rebellion, and the enemy grew weaker still.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦封燕、晉諸王為邊籓鎮，更歲遣大將巡行塞下，督諸衛卒屯田，戒以持重，寇來輒敗之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor also enfeoffed the princes of Yan, Jin, and others as frontier feudatories, and each year sent great generals to patrol below the passes, supervising garrison troops in colony fields, admonishing them to be steady, and whenever raiders came defeating them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor enfeoffed the princes of Yan and Jin as frontier lords, sent great generals yearly to patrol the border, supervised garrison farming, urged caution, and ordered raiders beaten back whenever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 而敵自脫古思帖木兒後，部帥紛拏，五傳至坤帖木兒，咸被弒，不復知帝號。

translations.literal: Among the enemy, after Togus Temür tribal chiefs contended in disorder; through five successions to Kuntiemuer all were assassinated and they no longer knew an imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: After Togus Temür the enemy chiefs fought among themselves; through five successions to Kuntiemuer each was murdered, and the imperial title was forgotten.

sentences.zh: 有鬼力赤者篡立，稱可汗，去國號，遂稱韃靼雲。

translations.literal: There was one Guilichi who usurped the throne, styled himself khan, discarded the dynastic title, and thereafter they were called Tartars.
translations.idiomatic: Guilichi seized power, styled himself khan, dropped the dynastic name, and thereafter they were known simply as Tartars.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，頭目埽胡兒、察罕達魯花等先後來歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle chieftains Saohu’er, Chahandaluhua, and others came to submit in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle three chieftains Saohu’er, Chahandaluhua, and others submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 久之，阿魯台殺鬼力赤，而迎元之後本雅失裡於別失八里，立為可汗。

translations.literal: After a long time Aruqtai killed Guilichi and welcomed the Yuan descendant Benyashili at Beshbalik, establishing him as khan.
translations.idiomatic: In time Aruqtai killed Guilichi, brought the Yuan heir Benyashili to Beshbalik, and set him up as khan.

sentences.zh: 六年春，帝即以書諭本雅失裡曰：「自元運既訖，順帝后愛猷識理達臘至坤帖木兒凡六傳，瞬息之間，未聞一人善終者。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the emperor immediately sent a letter instructing Benyashili, saying: “Since the Yuan mandate ended, from after Emperor Shun through Ayushiridara to Kuntiemuer there were six successions; in the blink of an eye not one is heard to have died a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the emperor wrote to Benyashili: “Since the Yuan mandate ended, from Emperor Shun through Ayushiridara to Kuntiemuer there were six successions—in that brief span not one is said to have died in his bed.

sentences.zh: 我皇考太祖高皇帝於元氏子孫，加意撫恤，來歸者輒令北還，如遣脫古思帖木兒歸，嗣為可汗，此南北人所共知。

translations.literal: My imperial father the founding High Emperor showed special care and comfort to Yuan descendants; those who came to submit were always sent back north, as when Togus Temür was sent back to succeed as khan—this is known alike north and south of the border.
translations.idiomatic: My father the founding emperor treated Yuan descendants with special kindness and sent those who submitted back north—as when he sent Togus Temür back to succeed as khan—a fact known on both sides of the border.

sentences.zh: 朕之心即皇考之心。

translations.literal: My heart is my imperial father’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is the same as my father’s.

sentences.zh: 茲元氏宗祧不絕如線，去就之機，禍福由分，爾宜審處之。」

translations.literal: Now the Yuan ancestral line hangs by a thread; the moment to stay or go, fortune or misfortune, lies in your own division—you should weigh it carefully.”
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan line now hangs by a thread; whether you stay or go, fortune or ruin, is yours to choose—weigh it carefully.”

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 明年，獲其部曲完者帖木兒等二十二人，帝因復使給事中郭驥齎書往。

translations.literal: The next year they captured twenty-two of his followers including Wanzhetiemuer; the emperor therefore again sent Supervising Secretary Guo Ji bearing a letter.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they captured twenty-two of his followers including Wanzhetiemuer, and the emperor again sent Supervising Secretary Guo Ji with a letter.

sentences.zh: 驥被殺，帝怒。

translations.literal: Ji was killed; the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was killed, and the emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 秋，命淇國公丘福為大將軍，武城侯王聰、同安侯火真副之，靖安侯王忠、安平侯李遠為左、右參將，將精騎十萬北討，諭以毋失機，毋輕犯敵，一舉未捷，俟再舉。

translations.literal: In autumn he appointed Duke of Qi Qiu Fu as grand general, with Marquis of Wucheng Wang Cong and Marquis of Tong’an Huozhen as his deputies and Marquis of Jing’an Wang Zhong and Marquis of Ping’an Li Yuan as left and right staff generals, leading one hundred thousand picked horsemen north to punish them, instructing them not to miss the opportunity, not to lightly engage the enemy, and if the first stroke did not succeed to wait for a second attempt.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he appointed Duke of Qi Qiu Fu grand general, with Wang Cong and Huozhen as deputies and Wang Zhong and Li Yuan as staff generals, and sent one hundred thousand picked cavalry north, warning them not to miss their chance, not to underestimate the enemy, and if the first strike failed to wait for another.

sentences.zh: 時本雅失裡已為瓦剌所襲破，與阿魯台徙居臚朐河。

translations.literal: At this time Benyashili had already been broken by an Oirat attack and with Aruqtai had moved to dwell on the Luqu River.
translations.idiomatic: By then Benyashili had already been shattered by the Oirats and had moved with Aruqtai to the Luqu River.

sentences.zh: 福率千騎先馳，遇游兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Fu led one thousand horsemen in a swift advance first and, encountering scouting troops, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led one thousand horse ahead at a gallop and routed enemy scouts.

sentences.zh: 軍未集，福乘勝渡河追敵，敵輒佯敗引去。

translations.literal: The army had not yet assembled; Fu, riding the victory, crossed the river in pursuit; the enemy repeatedly feigned defeat to draw him on.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army had gathered, Fu crossed the river in pursuit on the momentum of victory while the enemy feigned retreat to lure him on.

sentences.zh: 諸將以帝命止福，福不聽。

translations.literal: The generals, citing the emperor’s command, tried to stop Fu, but Fu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The generals cited the emperor’s orders to stop him, but Fu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 敵眾奄至，圍之，五將軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Enemy masses suddenly arrived and surrounded them; all five generals perished.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy forces suddenly surrounded them, and all five generals were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s anger deepened.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝自將五十萬眾出塞。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor personally led five hundred thousand men out beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor led five hundred thousand men beyond the passes in person.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡聞之懼，欲與阿魯台俱西，阿魯台不從，眾潰散，君臣始各為部。

translations.literal: Benyashili, hearing this, was afraid and wished to go west together with Aruqtai; Aruqtai would not follow; the masses scattered in defeat; ruler and ministers then each became a separate tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Benyashili, hearing this, was terrified and wanted to flee west with Aruqtai; Aruqtai refused; their forces scattered, and ruler and minister each became a separate faction.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡西奔，阿魯台東奔。

translations.literal: Benyashili fled west; Aruqtai fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Benyashili fled west and Aruqtai fled east.

sentences.zh: 帝追及斡難河，本雅失裡拒戰。

translations.literal: The emperor pursued to the Onon River; Benyashili resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor caught him on the Onon River, and Benyashili gave battle.

sentences.zh: 帝麾兵奮擊，一呼敗之。

translations.literal: The emperor waved his troops to strike fiercely; at one shout they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waved his troops forward in a fierce charge and broke them at a shout.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡棄輜重孳畜，以七騎遁。

translations.literal: Benyashili abandoned baggage and livestock and fled with seven horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Benyashili abandoned baggage and herds and escaped with seven riders.

sentences.zh: 斡難河者，元太祖始興地也。

translations.literal: The Onon River was the place where the Yuan founding ancestor first rose to power.
translations.idiomatic: The Onon was where the Yuan founding ancestor had first risen.

sentences.zh: 班師至靜虜鎮，遇阿魯台，帝使諭之降。

translations.literal: On the return march they reached Jinglu Town, encountered Aruqtai, and the emperor sent men to instruct him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal they reached Jinglu Town, met Aruqtai, and the emperor sent word urging him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台欲來，眾不可，遂戰。

translations.literal: Aruqtai wished to come, but his followers would not allow it, and so they fought.
translations.idiomatic: Aruqtai wished to come, but his followers refused, and battle followed.

sentences.zh: 帝率精騎大呼衝擊，矢下如注，阿魯台墜馬，遂大敗，追奔百餘里乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor led picked horsemen in a great-shouting charge; arrows fell like rain; Aruqtai fell from his horse; they were utterly defeated; the pursuit ran more than a hundred li before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led picked cavalry in a shouting charge; arrows fell like rain; Aruqtai was thrown from his horse; his force was shattered; the pursuit ran more than a hundred li before the Ming turned back.

sentences.zh: 冬，阿魯台使來貢馬，帝納之。

translations.literal: In winter Aruqtai’s envoys came to present horses in tribute; the emperor accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Aruqtai sent tribute horses, and the emperor accepted them.

sentences.zh: 越二年，本雅失裡為瓦剌馬哈木等所殺。

translations.literal: Two years later Benyashili was killed by the Oirat Mahamu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Benyashili was killed by the Oirat leader Mahamu and his followers.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台已數入貢，帝俱厚報之，並還其向所俘同產兄妹二人。

translations.literal: Aruqtai had already presented tribute several times; the emperor each time responded generously and also returned the two full siblings of his own blood whom he had formerly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Aruqtai had already sent tribute several times; the emperor had always rewarded him generously and now returned two siblings of his own blood whom the Ming had once captured.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏馬哈木等弒其主，又擅立答裡巴，願輸誠內附，請為故主復仇。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized that Mahamu and others had murdered their lord and had presumptuously set up Daliba, and he wished to offer sincere allegiance and submit inward, asking to avenge his former lord.
translations.idiomatic: He now reported that Mahamu and others had murdered their lord and set up Daliba on their own authority, offered sincere submission, and asked to avenge his former master.

sentences.zh: 天子義之，封為和寧王。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved his cause and enfeoffed him as Prince of Hening.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his cause and enfeoffed him as Prince of Hening.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲或一貢，或再貢，以為常。

translations.literal: From this time tribute came once or twice a year as a regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came once or twice a year as a matter of course.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝征瓦剌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor campaigned against the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor campaigned against the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台使部長以下來朝會。

translations.literal: Aruqtai sent tribal chiefs and those below them to attend the court assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Aruqtai sent his chiefs and subordinates to attend the court assembly.

sentences.zh: 賜米五十石，乾肉、酒糗、彩幣有差。

translations.literal: They were granted fifty piculs of grain, dried meat, wine, parched grain, and silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: They received fifty piculs of grain, dried meat, wine, parched grain, and silks in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以戰敗瓦剌，使來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because they had defeated the Oirats in battle, envoys came to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after defeating the Oirats in battle, they sent envoys with captives.

sentences.zh: 十九年，阿魯台貢使至邊，要劫行旅，帝諭使戒戢之，由是驕蹇不至。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Aruqtai’s tribute envoys reached the border and waylaid travelers; the emperor instructed the envoys to warn and restrain them; because of this they grew arrogant and obstinate and ceased coming.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Aruqtai’s tribute envoys waylaid travelers at the border; the emperor ordered them warned; thereafter they grew arrogant and stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台之內附，困於瓦剌，窮蹙而南，思假息塞外。

translations.literal: Aruqtai’s inward submission came because he was hard pressed by the Oirats, driven to extremity and moving south, thinking to borrow respite beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Aruqtai submitted because the Oirats had driven him to extremity in the south; he sought respite beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 帝納而封之，母妻皆為王太夫人、王夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted him and enfeoffed him; his mother and wife were both made Grand Lady and Lady of the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted him and enfeoffed him; his mother and wife were styled Grand Lady and Lady of the prince.

sentences.zh: 數年生聚，畜牧日以蕃盛，遂慢我使者，拘留之。

translations.literal: For several years they bred and gathered; livestock daily grew more abundant; they then slighted our envoys and detained them.
translations.idiomatic: For several years they bred stock and grew prosperous; then they slighted Ming envoys and detained them.

sentences.zh: 其貢使歸，多行劫掠，部落亦時來窺塞。

translations.literal: When their tribute envoys returned they often committed robbery and plunder; their tribes also from time to time came to spy on the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute envoys often raided on the return journey, and their tribes periodically probed the border passes.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，大人興和。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year they raided greatly at Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year they launched a major raid on Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 於是詔親征之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered a personal campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered a personal campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台聞大軍出，懼，其母妻皆詈之曰：「大明皇帝何負爾，而必為逆！」

translations.literal: Aruqtai, hearing the great army was marching out, was afraid; his mother and wife all reviled him, saying: “What has the Great Ming emperor done you wrong, that you must be rebellious!”
translations.idiomatic: When Aruqtai heard the great army was marching, he was afraid; his mother and wife reviled him: “What has the Ming emperor done you, that you must rebel!”

sentences.zh: 於是盡棄其輜重馬畜於闊灤海側，以其孥直北徙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abandoned all his baggage and livestock beside Kuoluanhai and moved his dependents due north.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned all baggage and herds beside Kuoluanhai and moved his family due north.

sentences.zh: 帝命焚其輜重，收其馬畜，遂班師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his baggage burned and his horses and livestock taken, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the baggage burned, the herds seized, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，邊將言阿魯台將入寇。

translations.literal: The next autumn frontier generals reported that Aruqtai was about to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn border commanders reported that Aruqtai was about to invade.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼意朕必不復出，當先駐塞下待之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “They think I will certainly not come out again; I should first encamp below the passes and wait for them.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “They think I will not march again—I shall camp below the passes and wait for them.”

sentences.zh: 遂部分寧陽侯陳懋為先鋒，至宿嵬山不見敵，遇王子也先土干率妻子部屬來降。

translations.literal: He then detached Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao as vanguard; reaching Suwei Mountain they saw no enemy; they encountered the prince Yexian Tugan leading his wife, children, and followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He detached Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao as vanguard; at Suwei Mountain they found no enemy but met Prince Yexian Tugan, who came to submit with his family and followers.

sentences.zh: 帝封為忠勇王，賜姓名曰金忠。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong and bestowed the surname and personal name Jin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong and gave him the Chinese name Jin Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠勇王至京師，數請擊敵自效。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhongyong reached the capital he repeatedly asked to strike the enemy and prove his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital, Prince Zhongyong repeatedly asked to strike the enemy and prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「姑待之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “For the present wait.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “Wait for now.”

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，開平守將奏阿魯台盜邊，群臣勸帝如忠勇王言。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the garrison commander of Kaiping memorialized that Aruqtai was raiding the border; the ministers urged the emperor to follow the Prince of Zhongyong’s advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year the Kaiping garrison reported Aruqtai raiding the border; the ministers urged the emperor to heed Prince Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 帝復親征，師次荅蘭納木兒河，得諜者，知阿魯台遠遁。

translations.literal: The emperor again campaigned in person; the army halted at the Tolan Namur River; spies were taken and it was learned that Aruqtai had fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor campaigned in person again; the army halted at the Tolan Namur River; spies revealed that Aruqtai had fled far away.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦厭兵，乃下詔暴阿魯台罪惡，而宥其所部來降者，止勿殺。

translations.literal: The emperor’s mind also wearied of war; he then issued an edict exposing Aruqtai’s crimes, yet pardoning those of his following who came to submit, ordering that they not be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had also grown weary of war; he issued an edict listing Aruqtai’s crimes but pardoning those who submitted and ordering that they not be killed.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，崩於榆木川。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned, and he died at Yumu River.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he died at Yumu River.

sentences.zh: 未幾，阿魯台使來貢馬，仁宗已登極，詔納之。

translations.literal: Before long Aruqtai’s envoys came to present horses in tribute; Renzong had already ascended the throne and ordered acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Aruqtai sent tribute horses; Renzong had already ascended the throne and ordered them accepted.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲修職貢如永樂時。

translations.literal: From this time yearly tribute was rendered as in the Yongle era.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter yearly tribute resumed as in the Yongle era.

sentences.zh: 時阿魯台數敗於瓦剌，部曲離散。

translations.literal: At this time Aruqtai had been repeatedly defeated by the Oirats and his followers were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Aruqtai had been repeatedly defeated by the Oirats and his followers were scattered.

sentences.zh: 其屬把的等先後來歸，朝廷皆予官職，賜鈔幣，詔有司給供具。

translations.literal: His followers Badi and others came to submit in succession; the court all granted them offices, bestowed paper money, and ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Badi and others submitted in succession; the court gave them offices, paper money, and orders to the ministries for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 自後來歸者，悉如例。

translations.literal: Those who came to submit afterward were all treated by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Later submitters were all treated by the same precedent.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台日益蹙，乃率其屬東走兀良哈，駐牧遼塞。

translations.literal: Aruqtai grew daily more pressed; he then led his followers east to the Uriyangqad and pastured on the Liao frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Growing ever more pressed, Aruqtai led his followers east to the Uriyangqad and pastured along the Liao frontier.

sentences.zh: 諸將請出兵掩擊之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The generals asked to send troops to strike them by surprise; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Generals asked to strike them by surprise; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 宣德九年，阿魯台復為脫脫不花所襲，妻子死，孳畜略盡，獨與其子失捏乾等徙居母納山、察罕腦剌等處。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xuande Aruqtai was again attacked by Toghon Temür; his wife and children died, his livestock were nearly all gone; he alone with his son Shiniegan and others moved to dwell at Muna Mountain, Chaghan Nao’er, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande nine Aruqtai was again attacked by Toghon Temür; his wife and children died and his herds were nearly gone; he fled with his son Shiniegan to Muna Mountain and Chaghan Nao’er.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瓦剌脫懽襲殺阿魯台及失捏干，於是阿魯檯子阿卜只俺及其孫妻速木答思等喪敗無依，來乞內附。

translations.literal: Before long the Oirat Toghon attacked and killed Aruqtai and Shiniegan; thereupon Aruqtai’s son Abuzhi’an and his grandson’s wife Sumudasi and others, defeated and without support, came begging to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Oirat Toghon killed Aruqtai and Shiniegan; Aruqtai’s son Abuzhi’an, his grandson’s wife Sumudasi, and others, defeated and homeless, came begging to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝憐而撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied them and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied them and received them kindly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，脫脫不花捕阿台等殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Toghon Temür captured Atai and others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Toghon Temür captured and killed Atai and his followers.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花者，故元後，韃靼長也。

translations.literal: Toghon Temür was a descendant of the former Yuan and chief of the Tartars.
translations.idiomatic: Toghon Temür was a Yuan descendant and chief of the Tartars.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌脫忄雚既擊殺阿魯台，悉收其部，兼併賢義、安樂二王之眾，欲自立為可汗。

translations.literal: The Oirat Toghon, having attacked and killed Aruqtai, wholly took over his following, merged the hosts of the princes of Xianyi and Anle, and wished to set himself up as khan.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirat Toghon, having killed Aruqtai, absorbed his following and merged the forces of the princes of Xianyi and Anle, and wished to proclaim himself khan.

sentences.zh: 眾不可，乃立脫脫不花，以阿魯台眾屬之，自為丞相，陽推奉之，實不承其號令。

translations.literal: The masses would not allow it; he then set up Toghon Temür, assigned Aruqtai’s followers to him, made himself chancellor, outwardly deferred to him, but in fact did not obey his commands.
translations.idiomatic: His followers would not allow it; he set up Toghon Temür, assigned Aruqtai’s people to him, styled himself chancellor, paid him outward deference, but did not obey his orders.

sentences.zh: 脫懽死，子也先嗣，益桀驁自雄，諸部皆下之，脫脫不花具可汗名而已。

translations.literal: Toghon died; his son Esen succeeded; he grew ever more fierce and proud, and all tribes submitted to him; Toghon Temür bore only the name of khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Toghon died his son Esen succeeded, grew ever more arrogant, and brought all tribes under him; Toghon Temür held only the title of khan.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花歲來朝貢，天子皆厚報之，比諸蕃有加，書稱之曰達達可汗，賜賚並及其妃。

translations.literal: Toghon Temür came yearly to court with tribute; the Son of Heaven each time responded generously, with more than for other foreign states; letters addressed him as Khan of the Tartars, and gifts were bestowed on his consort as well.
translations.idiomatic: Toghon Temür came to court with tribute each year; the emperor rewarded him more generously than other foreign states, addressed him in writing as Khan of the Tartars, and bestowed gifts on his consort as well.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，也先謀大舉入寇，脫脫不花止之曰：「吾儕服食，多資大明，何忍為此？」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year Esen planned a great invasion; Toghon Temür stopped him, saying: “Our clothing and food depend largely on the Great Ming—how can we bear to do this?”
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year Esen planned a major invasion; Toghon Temür stopped him: “Our clothing and food come largely from the Ming—how can we bear to do this?”

sentences.zh: 也先不聽，曰：「可汗不為，吾當自為。」

translations.literal: Esen would not listen and said: “If the khan will not do it, I shall do it myself.”
translations.idiomatic: Esen would not listen: “If the khan will not act, I shall act myself.”

sentences.zh: 遂分道，俾脫脫不花侵遼東，而自擁眾從大同入。

translations.literal: They then divided their routes, ordering Toghon Temür to invade Liaodong while he himself with his host entered by Datong.
translations.idiomatic: They split forces: Toghon Temür was to raid Liaodong while Esen led his host in through Datong.

sentences.zh: 帝親征之，駕於土木陷焉。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned in person and was trapped at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched in person and was trapped at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝自監國即位，尊帝為太上皇帝。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor, having ruled as regent, ascended the throne and honored the emperor as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor, who had ruled as regent, ascended the throne and honored the captive emperor as Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，上皇歸自也先所。

translations.literal: The next autumn the retired emperor returned from Esen’s custody.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the retired emperor returned from Esen’s custody.

sentences.zh: 事載《瓦剌傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the “Biography of the Oirats.”
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in the biography of the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花自上皇歸後，修貢益勤。

translations.literal: After the retired emperor’s return Toghon Temür rendered tribute ever more diligently.
translations.idiomatic: After the retired emperor’s return Toghon Temür sent tribute ever more diligently.

sentences.zh: 嘗妻也先姊，生子，也先欲立之，不從。

translations.literal: He had once married Esen’s elder sister and had a son; Esen wished to set him up as heir, but he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He had married Esen’s elder sister and had a son; Esen wished to set the boy up as heir, but Toghon Temür refused.

sentences.zh: 也先亦疑其與中國通，將害己，遂治兵相攻。

translations.literal: Esen also suspected that he was in communication with China and would harm him; he then arrayed troops and they attacked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Esen also suspected him of colluding with China and plotting against him; they arrayed troops and fought.

sentences.zh: 也先殺脫脫不花，收其妻子孳畜，給諸部屬，而自立為可汗。

translations.literal: Esen killed Toghon Temür, took his wife, children, and livestock, distributed them among the tribal followers, and set himself up as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Esen killed Toghon Temür, seized his family and herds, distributed them among his followers, and proclaimed himself khan.

sentences.zh: 時景皇帝二年也。

translations.literal: This was in the second year of the Jing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second year of the Jing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷稱也先為瓦剌可汗。

translations.literal: The court styled Esen Khan of the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: The court styled Esen Khan of the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為所部阿剌知院所殺。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed by his follower Alag Zhihui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his follower Alag Zhihui killed him.

sentences.zh: 韃靼部長孛來復攻破阿剌，求脫脫不花子麻兒可兒立之，號小王子。

translations.literal: The Tartar chief Bolai again defeated Alag, sought Toghon Temür’s son Markö’er and set him up, styling him the Little Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartar chief Bolai defeated Alag, found Toghon Temür’s son Markö’er, and set him up as the Little Prince.

sentences.zh: 阿剌死，而孛來與其屬毛裡孩等皆雄視部中，於是韃靼復熾。

translations.literal: Alag died, and Bolai with his follower Maolihai and others all dominated the tribe; the Tartars then grew strong again.
translations.idiomatic: When Alag died, Bolai and his follower Maolihai dominated the tribes, and the Tartars grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai envoys were sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai six they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，遣都督馬政往賜故伯顏帖木兒妻幣。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored the throne he sent Regional Commander Ma Zheng to bestow silks on the former wife of Bayan Temür.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong restored the throne he sent Regional Commander Ma Zheng with silks for Bayan Temür’s former wife.

sentences.zh: 孛來留之，而遣使入賀，欲獻璽。

translations.literal: Bolai detained him but sent envoys to offer congratulations and wished to present the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai detained him but sent envoys to congratulate the emperor and offered to present the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 帝敕之曰：「璽已非真，即真，亦秦不祥物耳，獻否從爾便。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed them, saying: “The seal is already not genuine; even if genuine, it is also an unlucky object of Qin—whether you present it or not is as you please.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: “The seal is already not genuine; even if it were, it is Qin’s ill-omened object—present it or not as you please.

sentences.zh: 第無留我使，以速爾禍。」

translations.literal: Only do not detain my envoy, lest you hasten your own disaster.”
translations.idiomatic: Only do not detain my envoy, lest you hasten your own ruin.”

sentences.zh: 時敵數寇威遠諸衛，夏，定遠伯石彪敗之於磨兒山。

translations.literal: At this time the enemy repeatedly raided the guards of Weiyuan and elsewhere; in summer Earl of Dingyuan Shi Biao defeated them at Mo’er Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy repeatedly raided the Weiyuan guards; that summer Earl of Dingyuan Shi Biao defeated them at Mo’er Mountain.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，孛來大舉寇陝西，安遠侯柳溥御之輒敗，而飾小捷以聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun Bolai raided Shaanxi in force; Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu met him and was repeatedly defeated, yet reported small victories.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun two Bolai raided Shaanxi in force; Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu was repeatedly beaten but reported minor victories.

sentences.zh: 明年春，敵入安邊營，石彪等破之，都督周賢、指揮李钅監戰死。

translations.literal: The next spring the enemy entered Anbian Camp; Shi Biao and others defeated them; Regional Commander Zhou Xian and Commander Li Jian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the enemy entered Anbian Camp; Shi Biao and others defeated them, but Regional Commander Zhou Xian and Commander Li Jian were killed.

sentences.zh: 四年復寇榆林，彰武伯楊信拒卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again raided Yulin; Earl of Zhangwu Yang Xin repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they raided Yulin again; Earl of Zhangwu Yang Xin drove them off.

sentences.zh: 再入，敗之於金雞峪。

translations.literal: They entered again and were defeated at Jinji Valley.
translations.idiomatic: They entered again and were defeated at Jinji Valley.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復大掠陝西諸邊，廷臣請治各守將罪，帝宥之。

translations.literal: Before long they again raided greatly along the Shaanxi frontier; court ministers asked that the defending generals be punished, but the emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they raided the Shaanxi frontier again; ministers asked that the border generals be punished, but the emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 五年春，寇入平虜城，誘指揮許顒等入伏，殺之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year raiders entered Pinglu City, lured Commander Xu Yong and others into an ambush, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year raiders entered Pinglu City, lured Commander Xu Yong and others into an ambush, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 邊報日亟，命侍郎白圭、都御史王竑往視師。

translations.literal: Frontier reports grew daily more urgent; Vice Minister Bai Gui and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong were ordered to go inspect the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier reports grew urgent daily; Vice Minister Bai Gui and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong were sent to inspect the armies.

sentences.zh: 秋，孛來求款，帝使詹升齎敕往諭。

translations.literal: In autumn Bolai sought peace; the emperor sent Zhan Sheng bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Bolai sought peace; the emperor sent Zhan Sheng with an edict.

sentences.zh: 孛來遣使隨升來貢，請改大同舊貢道，而由陝西蘭縣入，許之。

translations.literal: Bolai sent envoys to follow Sheng with tribute, asking to change from the old tribute route through Datong and enter by Lan County in Shaanxi; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai sent envoys with Sheng bearing tribute, asking to enter by Lan County in Shaanxi instead of the old Datong route; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復糾其屬毛裡孩等入河西。

translations.literal: Before long he again gathered his follower Maolihai and others to enter Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again led Maolihai and others into Hexi.

sentences.zh: 明年春，圭等分巡西邊，圭遇敵於固原川，竑遇敵於紅崖子川，皆破之。

translations.literal: The next spring Gui and the others patrolled the western frontier separately; Gui met the enemy at Guyuan River and Hong defeated them at Hongyazi River; both were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Gui and the others patrolled the west separately; Gui defeated the enemy at Guyuan River and Wang Hong at Hongyazi River.

sentences.zh: 帝賜璽書獎勵，敕孛來使臣仍從大同入貢。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a sealed letter of commendation and ordered Bolai’s envoys again to enter tribute by Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a sealed letter of commendation and ordered Bolai’s envoys to resume entering tribute by Datong.

sentences.zh: 時麻兒可兒復與孛來相仇殺。

translations.literal: At this time Markö’er again feuded and fought with Bolai.
translations.idiomatic: Markö’er and Bolai were feuding and fighting again.

sentences.zh: 麻兒可兒死，眾共立馬可古兒吉思，亦號小王子。

translations.literal: Markö’er died; the masses jointly set up Makugürjis, who was also styled the Little Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Markö’er died the tribes set up Makugürjis, also styled the Little Prince.

sentences.zh: 自是，韃靼部長益各專擅。

translations.literal: From this time Tartar chiefs increasingly each held sole power.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tartar chiefs increasingly ruled their own domains.

sentences.zh: 小王子稀通中國，傳世次，多莫可考。

translations.literal: The Little Prince rarely communicated with China; the succession is largely beyond verification.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince rarely had contact with China; the succession is largely unverifiable.

sentences.zh: 孛來等每歲入貢，數寇掠，往來塞下，以西攻瓦剌為辭，又數要劫三衛。

translations.literal: Bolai and others presented tribute yearly yet repeatedly raided, moving back and forth below the passes, using attacks on the Oirats in the west as a pretext, and also repeatedly waylaid the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai and others sent yearly tribute yet raided repeatedly, moving below the passes, citing campaigns against the western Oirats, and repeatedly waylaid the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，貢使及關，帝卻之，以大學士李賢言乃止。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year tribute envoys reached the pass; the emperor turned them back, and only because Grand Secretary Li Xian spoke did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year tribute envoys reached the pass; the emperor turned them back and only stopped when Grand Secretary Li Xian intervened.

sentences.zh: 八年春，御史陳選言：「韃靼部落，孛來最強，又密招三衛諸蕃，相結屯住。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year Censor Chen Xuan said: “Among the Tartar tribes Bolai is strongest; he has also secretly summoned the various peoples of the Three Guards to join and encamp together.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year Censor Chen Xuan said: “Among the Tartar tribes Bolai is strongest; he has secretly summoned the Three Guards peoples to camp together with him.

sentences.zh: 去冬來朝，要我賞宴，窺我虛實，其犯邊之情已露。

translations.literal: Last winter he came to court, demanded rewards and banquets from us, spied on our strength and weakness—his intent to violate the border is already exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter he came to court, demanded rewards and banquets, and spied on our strength—his intent to raid is already clear.

sentences.zh: 而我邊關守臣，因循怠慢，城堡不修，甲仗不利，軍士不操習，甚至富者納月錢而安閒，貧者迫飢寒而逃竄。

translations.literal: Yet our frontier defending officials are complacent and negligent; fortresses are not repaired; arms are not effective; soldiers are not drilled; some wealthy men pay monthly fees and live at ease, while the poor, driven by hunger and cold, flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our border officials are complacent; fortresses are unrepaired, arms poor, and troops undrilled; the rich pay monthly fees to live at ease while the poor flee hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 邊備廢弛，緩急何恃？

translations.literal: Frontier defenses are neglected—on what can we rely in emergency?
translations.idiomatic: With frontier defenses neglected, what can we rely on in an emergency?

sentences.zh: 乞敕在邊諸臣，痛革前弊。

translations.literal: I beg that frontier officials be ordered to reform past abuses thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that frontier officials be ordered to reform these abuses thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 其鎮守、備御等官，亦宜以時黜陟，庶能者知奮，怠者知警。

translations.literal: Garrison, defense, and other officials should also be promoted or demoted in due season, so that the capable know to strive and the idle know to beware.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison and defense officials should be promoted or demoted in due season so the capable strive and the idle take warning.

sentences.zh: 至厄塞要害之處，或益官軍，或設營堡，或用墩台，咸須處置得宜，歲遣大臣巡視，庶邊防有備，寇氛可戢。」

translations.literal: As for strategic passes and vital points, whether by increasing official troops, establishing camps and forts, or using beacon towers, all must be disposed properly; yearly send great ministers to inspect, so that the frontier may be prepared and raider unrest quelled.”
translations.idiomatic: At strategic passes we should add troops, build forts, or use beacon towers as needed, send ministers yearly to inspect, and so keep the frontier prepared and raiders in check.”

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 成化元年春，孛來誘兀良哈九萬騎入遼河，武安侯鄭宏御卻之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Chenghua Bolai induced ninety thousand Uriyangqad horsemen to enter the Liao River; Marquis of Wu’an Zheng Hong repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Chenghua one Bolai induced ninety thousand Uriyangqad horsemen into the Liao River; Marquis of Wu’an Zheng Hong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 秋，散掠延綏。

translations.literal: In autumn they scattered in raids on Yan–Sui.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they scattered in raids across Yan–Sui.

sentences.zh: 冬，復大入。

translations.literal: In winter they again raided in force.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they again invaded in force.

sentences.zh: 命彰武伯楊信率山西兵，都御史項忠率陝西兵御之，少卻。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Marquis of Zhangwu Yang Xin to lead Shanxi troops and Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong to lead Shaanxi troops to repel them; the enemy withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Marquis of Zhangwu Yang Xin with Shanxi troops and Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong with Shaanxi troops to meet them; the raiders withdrew slightly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復渡河曲，圍黃甫川堡，官軍力戰，乃引去。

translations.literal: Before long they again crossed the river bend, besieged Huangfuchuan Fort, and only withdrew after government troops fought hard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they crossed the river bend again, besieged Huangfuchuan Fort, and withdrew only after a hard fight by government troops.

sentences.zh: 始，韃靼之來也，或在遼東、宣府、大同，或在寧夏、莊浪、甘肅，去來無常，為患不久。

translations.literal: At first when the Tartars came, they might appear in Liaodong, Xuanfu, or Datong, or in Ningxia, Zhuanglang, or Gansu; their comings and goings were unpredictable and the trouble did not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tartar raids struck Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, or Ningxia, Zhuanglang, and Gansu unpredictably, and rarely persisted long.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，始犯延慶，然部落少，不敢深入。

translations.literal: In the early Jingtai era they first struck Yanqing, but their tribes were few and they did not dare penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jingtai they first raided Yanqing, but with few tribes they did not dare push far inland.

sentences.zh: 天順間，有阿羅出者，率屬潛入河套居之，遂逼近西邊。

translations.literal: During the Tianshun era a man named Alach led his followers secretly into the Ordos Loop to dwell there, thus pressing close to the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshun a leader named Alach led his followers secretly into the Ordos to settle, drawing nearer the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 河套，古朔方郡，唐張仁願築三受降城處也。

translations.literal: The Ordos Loop was ancient Shuofang commandery, the place where Tang Zhang Renyuan built the three Accept-the-Submission cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos was ancient Shuofang commandery, where Tang Zhang Renyuan had built the three Accept-the-Submission fortresses.

sentences.zh: 地在黃河南，自寧夏至偏頭關，延袤二千里，饒水草，外為東勝衛。

translations.literal: The land lay south of the Yellow River, stretching two thousand li from Ningxia to Piantou Pass, rich in grass and water; beyond it lay Dongsheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River it ran two thousand li from Ningxia to Piantou Pass, rich in pasture; Dongsheng Guard lay beyond it.

sentences.zh: 東勝而外，土平衍，敵來，一騎不能隱，明初守之，後以曠絕內徙。

translations.literal: Beyond Dongsheng the land was flat and open; when enemies came, not a single horseman could hide; in early Ming it was garrisoned, but later because of its desolation the garrisons were moved inward.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Dongsheng the country was flat and open, hiding no rider; the Ming garrisoned it early on, but later withdrew inward as the land fell empty.

sentences.zh: 至是，孛來與小王子、毛裡孩等先後繼至，擄中國人為鄉導，抄掠延綏無虛時，而邊事以棘。

translations.literal: At this point Bolai, the Little Prince, Maolihai, and others arrived in succession one after another, seized Chinese as guides, and plundered Yan–Sui without respite; frontier affairs grew acute.
translations.idiomatic: Then Bolai, the Little Prince, Maolihai, and others arrived in turn, taking Chinese captives as guides and plundering Yan–Sui without pause, and the frontier crisis deepened.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，大入延綏。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year they raided Yan–Sui in force.
translations.idiomatic: That summer they launched a major raid on Yan–Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝命楊信充總兵官，都督趙勝為副，率京軍及諸邊卒二萬人討之。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Yang Xin commander-in-chief, with Commander Zhao Sheng as deputy, to lead twenty thousand capital troops and frontier soldiers against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Yang Xin commander-in-chief and Zhao Sheng his deputy, sending twenty thousand capital and frontier troops against them.

sentences.zh: 信先以議事赴闕，未至。

translations.literal: Xin had first gone to court on business and had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin had gone to court on other business and had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 敵散掠平涼，入靈州及固原，長驅寇靜寧、隆德諸處。

translations.literal: The enemy scattered in raids on Pingliang, entered Lingzhou and Guyuan, and drove deep to strike Jingning, Longde, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders scattered across Pingliang, entered Lingzhou and Guyuan, and drove deep into Jingning, Longde, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 冬，復入延綏，參將湯胤績戰死。

translations.literal: In winter they again entered Yan–Sui; Regiment Commander Tang Yinji died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they raided Yan–Sui again; Regiment Commander Tang Yinji was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸部內爭，孛來弒馬可古兒吉思，毛裡孩殺孛來，更立他可汗。

translations.literal: Before long the tribes quarreled among themselves; Bolai assassinated Makugürjis, Maolihai killed Bolai, and they set up another khan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the tribes turned on one another: Bolai murdered Makugürjis, Maolihai killed Bolai, and another khan was installed.

sentences.zh: 斡羅出者復與毛裡孩相仇殺，毛裡孩遂殺其所立可汗，逐斡羅出，而遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Oloroo again feuded and fought with Maolihai; Maolihai then killed the khan he had set up, drove out Oloroo, and sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Oloroo feuded with Maolihai again; Maolihai killed the khan he had installed, expelled Oloroo, and sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 尋渡河掠大同。

translations.literal: Before long they crossed the river and plundered Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they crossed the river and raided Datong.

sentences.zh: 三年春，帝命撫寧侯硃永等征之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the emperor ordered Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor ordered Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong and others to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 會毛裡孩再乞通貢，而別部長孛魯乃亦遣人來朝。

translations.literal: Just then Maolihai again begged to resume tribute, and Belunai, chief of another branch, also sent men to court.
translations.idiomatic: Maolihai again petitioned to resume tribute, and Belunai of another branch also sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，詔永等駐軍塞上。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this and ordered Yong and the others to encamp their armies on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Zhu Yong and the others to keep their armies on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，給事中程萬里上言：「毛裡孩久不朝貢，窺伺邊疆，其情叵測。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year Supervising Secretary Cheng Wanli memorialized: “Maolihai has long failed to come to court with tribute and watches our frontier; his intentions are impossible to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Supervising Secretary Cheng Wanli wrote: “Maolihai has long stopped sending tribute and watches our borders; his intentions are hard to read.

sentences.zh: 然臣度其有可敗者三。

translations.literal: Yet your servant considers that he has three points by which he can be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see three reasons he can be beaten.

sentences.zh: 近我邊地才二三日程，彼客我主，一也。

translations.literal: Our frontier is only two or three days’ march away; he is the guest and we the host — that is the first.
translations.idiomatic: First, our border is only two or three days’ march away — he is the intruder on our ground.

sentences.zh: 兼併諸部，馳驅不息，既驕且疲，二也。

translations.literal: He has swallowed other tribes and rides without rest; he is both arrogant and weary — that is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, his endless consolidation and raiding have made him arrogant and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 比來散逐水草，部落四分，兵力不一，三也。

translations.literal: Lately they have scattered to follow grass and water; the tribes are split four ways and their strength is not united — that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, they have lately scattered after pasture, splitting into factions whose strength is no longer united.

sentences.zh: 宜選精兵二萬，每三千人為一軍，統以驍將，嚴其賞罰，使探毛裡孩所在，潛師搗之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Choose twenty thousand picked troops, form an army of three thousand men each under dashing generals, enforce rewards and punishments strictly, find where Maolihai is, and strike him with a hidden force — he is sure to be broken.”
translations.idiomatic: Send twenty thousand picked troops in formations of three thousand under bold generals, enforce discipline, locate Maolihai, and strike by surprise — he will surely be broken.”

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，而不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the plan but could not put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan but did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 冬寇延綏。

translations.literal: In winter they raided Yan–Sui.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they raided Yan–Sui.

sentences.zh: 明年春再入。

translations.literal: The next spring they entered again.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring they invaded again.

sentences.zh: 守將許寧等輒擊敗之。

translations.literal: The defending generals Xu Ning and others promptly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Defending generals Xu Ning and others promptly beat them back.

sentences.zh: 冬復糾三衛入寇，延綏、榆林大擾。

translations.literal: In winter they again gathered the Three Guards and invaded; Yan–Sui and Yulin were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they rallied the Three Guards and invaded, wreaking havoc in Yan–Sui and Yulin.

sentences.zh: 六年春，大同巡撫王越遣游擊許寧擊敗之；

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Grand Coordinator of Datong Wang Yue sent Regiment Commander Xu Ning and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Grand Coordinator Wang Yue of Datong sent Regiment Commander Xu Ning and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 楊信等亦大破之於胡柴氵冓。

translations.literal: Yang Xin and others also broke them decisively at Huchai Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin and others also won a decisive victory at Huchai Gan.

sentences.zh: 時孛魯乃與斡羅出合別部加思蘭、孛羅忽亦入據河套，為久居計。

translations.literal: At this time Belunai joined Oloroo and chiefs of other branches, Boluosilan and Beluohu, also entered and occupied the Ordos, intending to stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Belunai and Oloroo allied with chiefs of other branches, Boluosilan and Beluohu, who also entered the Ordos to settle for the long term.

sentences.zh: 延綏告急，帝命永為將軍，以王越參贊軍務，使禦敵。

translations.literal: Yan–Sui sent urgent reports; the emperor appointed Yong general, with Wang Yue to assist in military affairs, to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan–Sui in crisis the emperor made Zhu Yong general and Wang Yue his aide to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 永至，數以捷聞，越等皆升賞，論功永世侯，而敵據套自如。

translations.literal: When Yong arrived, repeated victories were reported; Yue and the others were all promoted and rewarded, and Yong was ennobled hereditary marquis for merit, yet the enemy still held the Loop as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong reported victory after victory; Yue and others were promoted, and Yong was made hereditary marquis for his service — yet the enemy still held the Ordos.

sentences.zh: 七年春，永上戰守二策，廷議以糧匱馬乏，難於進剿，請命邊將慎守禦以圖萬全。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Yong submitted plans for both attack and defense; court discussion held that grain was scarce and horses exhausted, making advance difficult, and asked that frontier generals guard carefully to seek complete security.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zhu Yong proposed plans for attack and defense; the court judged supplies and horses too scarce for an offensive and ordered careful frontier defense instead.

sentences.zh: 於是吏部侍郎葉盛巡邊，偕延綏巡撫餘子俊及越議築邊牆，設立台堡。
