translations.idiomatic: That winter they attacked Fenghuang City again; Hei Chun fought for two days and nights and was killed.

sentences.zh: 海、金殺掠尤甚。

translations.literal: At Hai and Jin the killing and plundering were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Hai and Jin suffered especially heavy killing and looting.

sentences.zh: 冬，俺答數犯山西、寧夏塞。

translations.literal: In winter Altan Khan raided the frontiers of Shanxi and Ningxia several times.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Altan Khan struck the Shanxi and Ningxia frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 延綏總兵趙岢分部銳卒，令裨將李希靖等東出神木堡，搗敵帳於半坡山，徐執中等西出定邊營，擊敵騎於荍麥湖，皆勝之，斬一百十九級。

translations.literal: Yan–Sui Commander-in-Chief Zhao Ke divided his picked troops, sent Lieutenant General Li Xijing and others east out of Shenmu Fort to strike the enemy camp at Banpo Mountain, and Xu Zhizhong and others west out of Dingbian Camp to attack enemy horsemen at Qiaomai Lake; all were victorious and took one hundred nineteen heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yan–Sui Commander Zhao Ke split his elite troops: Lieutenant General Li Xijing marched east from Shenmu Fort and raided the enemy camp at Banpo Mountain, while Xu Zhizhong marched west from Dingbian Camp and struck enemy horsemen at Qiaomai Lake; both columns won, taking one hundred nineteen heads.

sentences.zh: 四十二年春，敵入宣府滴水崖，劉漢卻之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the forty-second year the enemy entered Dishui Cliff of Xuanfu; Liu Han drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, spring, the raiders entered Dishui Cliff in Xuanfu; Liu Han drove them off.

sentences.zh: 敵遂引而東，數犯遼塞。

translations.literal: The enemy then withdrew eastward and raided the Liaodong frontier several times.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders then shifted east and struck the Liaodong frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 秋，總兵楊照敗死。

translations.literal: In autumn Commander-in-Chief Yang Zhao was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Commander Yang Zhao was killed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 時薊遼總督楊選囚縶三衛長通罕，令其諸子更迭為質。

translations.literal: At that time Ji–Liao Governor-General Yang Xuan imprisoned Tonghan, chief of the Three Guards, and had his sons take turns serving as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Ji–Liao Governor-General Yang Xuan then imprisoned Tonghan, chief of the Three Guards, and kept his sons as rotating hostages.

sentences.zh: 通罕者，辛愛妻父也，冀以牽制辛愛，三衛皆怨。

translations.literal: Tonghan was Engi's wife's father; they hoped thereby to restrain Engi, but all Three Guards resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghan was Engi's father-in-law; the court hoped to use him to restrain Engi, but all Three Guards were resentful.

sentences.zh: 冬，大掠順義、三河。

translations.literal: In winter they plundered Shunyi and Sanhe on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they looted Shunyi and Sanhe on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 諸將趙溱、孫臏戰死，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: Generals Zhao Qin and Sun Bin died in battle, and the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Zhao Qin and Sun Bin were killed, and the capital went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 大同總兵姜應熊御之於密雲，敗之，敵退。

translations.literal: Datong Commander-in-Chief Jiang Yingxiong met them at Miyun, defeated them, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Datong Commander Jiang Yingxiong met them at Miyun, routed them, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔誅選。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xuan executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yang Xuan executed.

sentences.zh: 明年，土蠻入遼東，都御史劉燾上諸將守禦功，言海水暴漲，敵騎多沒者。

translations.literal: The next year Tümen entered Liaodong; Censor-in-Chief Liu Tao submitted the defensive achievements of the generals, saying the sea water rose violently and many enemy horsemen were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Tümen entered Liaodong; Censor-in-Chief Liu Tao reported the generals' defensive successes, noting that a sudden surge of seawater had drowned many raiders.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「海若效靈。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The sea god has shown its efficacy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The sea god has shown its power."

sentences.zh: 下有司祭告，燾等皆有賞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices were ordered to offer sacrifices and report; Liu Tao and the others were all rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the relevant offices to offer sacrifices and report back; Liu Tao and the others were all rewarded.

sentences.zh: 冬，敵犯狹西，大掠板橋、響閘兒諸處。

translations.literal: In winter the enemy raided Shaanxi and plundered Banqiao, Xiangzhai'er, and other places on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the raiders struck Shaanxi and looted Banqiao, Xiangzhai'er, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 四十四年春，犯遼東寧前小團山，參將線補袞、游擊楊維籓死之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the forty-fourth year they raided Xiaotuanshan in Ningqian, Liaodong; Regimental Commander Xian Bugun and Brigadier Yang Weifan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year, spring, they struck Xiaotuanshan in eastern Liaodong; Regimental Commander Xian Bugun and Brigadier Yang Weifan were killed.

sentences.zh: 夏，犯肅州，總兵劉承業御之，再戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In summer they raided Suzhou; Commander-in-Chief Liu Chengye met them and won victory in both battles.
translations.idiomatic: That summer they struck Suzhou; Commander Liu Chengye met them and won both engagements.

sentences.zh: 秋，俺答子黃台吉帥輕騎，自宣府洗馬林突入，散掠內地。

translations.literal: In autumn Altan Khan's son Huang Taiji led light horsemen, burst in from Ximolin of Xuanfu, and plundered freely across the interior.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Huang Taiji, Altan Khan's son, led light cavalry in a sudden thrust from Ximolin in Xuanfu and looted the interior at will.

sentences.zh: 把總姜汝棟以銳卒二百伏暗莊堡，猝遇台吉，搏之。

translations.literal: Detachment Commander Jiang Rudong with two hundred picked soldiers lay in ambush at Anzhuang Fort, suddenly encountered Taiji, and grappled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Detachment Commander Jiang Rudong lay in wait at Anzhuang Fort with two hundred elite troops, suddenly encountered Huang Taiji, and closed with him hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 台吉墮馬，為所部奪去。

translations.literal: Taiji fell from his horse and was carried off by his own followers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji was unhorsed and swept away by his own men.

sentences.zh: 台吉受傷，越日始蘇。

translations.literal: Taiji was wounded and only recovered consciousness the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji was badly hurt and did not regain consciousness until the following day.

sentences.zh: 明年，俺答屢犯東西諸塞。

translations.literal: The next year Altan Khan repeatedly violated the eastern and western frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Altan Khan raided the eastern and western border passes again and again.

sentences.zh: 夏，清河守備郎得功扼之張能峪口，勝之。

translations.literal: In summer the Qinghe garrison commander Lang Degong blocked him at Zhangneng Pass and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Garrison Commander Lang Degong of Qinghe intercepted him at Zhangneng Pass and won the day.

sentences.zh: 冬，大同參將崔世榮禦敵於樊皮嶺，及子大朝、大賓俱戰死。

translations.literal: In winter Datong Regimental Commander Cui Shirong met the enemy at Fanpi Ridge; he and his sons Dachao and Dabin all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Regimental Commander Cui Shirong of Datong fought the enemy at Fanpi Ridge and fell, along with his sons Dachao and Dabin.

sentences.zh: 時丘富死，趙全在敵中益用事，尊俺答為帝，治宮殿。

translations.literal: At this time Qiu Fu died; Zhao Quan among the enemy came to wield even greater power, honoring Altan Khan as emperor and building palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu had died by then, and Zhao Quan grew ever more influential among the Mongols, styling Altan Khan as emperor and erecting palaces for him.

sentences.zh: 期日上棟，忽大風，棟墜傷數人。

translations.literal: On the day fixed for raising the ridgepole, a sudden great wind blew; the ridgepole fell and injured several men.
translations.idiomatic: On the day set for raising the ridgepole, a sudden gale struck; the beam crashed down and injured several men.

sentences.zh: 俺答懼，不敢復居。

translations.literal: Altan Khan was afraid and did not dare live there again.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan was shaken and never dared occupy the palace again.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎譚綸在薊鎮善治兵，全乃說俺答無輕犯薊，大同兵弱，可以逞。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Tan Lun was good at training troops in the Ji garrison; Quan then advised Altan Khan not to raid Ji lightly—the Datong garrison was weak and he could make free there.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Tan Lun was rebuilding the Ji garrison's fighting strength; Quan urged Altan Khan to leave Ji alone and strike Datong instead, where the garrison was weak enough to plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 二年，敵犯柴溝，守備韓尚忠戰死。

translations.literal: In the second year the enemy raided Chaigou; Garrison Commander Han Shangzhong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the raiders struck Chaigou; Garrison Commander Han Shangzhong was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 時兵部侍郎王崇古鎮西邊，總兵李成梁守遼東，數以兵邀擊於塞外。

translations.literal: At this time Vice Minister of War Wang Chonggu commanded the western frontier and Commander-in-Chief Li Chengliang held Liaodong; repeatedly they intercepted the enemy with troops beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu was then overseeing the western frontier as vice minister of war, while Li Chengliang held Liaodong; again and again they ambushed raiders beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 敵知有備，入寇稍稀。

translations.literal: The enemy knew there were preparations and invasions became somewhat less frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the raiders found the frontier prepared, their incursions grew less frequent.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，黃台吉寇錦州，總兵王治道、參將郎得功以十餘騎入敵死。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year Huang Taiji raided Jinzhou; Commander-in-Chief Wang Zhidao and Regimental Commander Lang Degong entered the enemy with a little more than ten horsemen and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, autumn, Huang Taiji struck Jinzhou; Commander Wang Zhidao and Regimental Commander Lang Degong charged into the enemy with barely a dozen riders and were killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，俺答有孫曰把漢那吉者，俺答第三子鐵背台吉子也，幼孤，育於俺答妻所。

translations.literal: In winter Altan Khan had a grandson called Bahannaji, the son of Altan Khan's third son Tiebei Taiji; orphaned young, he was reared in the household of Altan Khan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: That winter: Altan Khan's grandson Bahannaji, son of his third son Tiebei Taiji, had lost his parents young and was raised in Altan Khan's wife's household.

sentences.zh: 既長，娶婦比吉。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he took Bigi as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he married a woman named Bigi.

sentences.zh: 把漢復聘襖兒都司女，即俺答外孫女，貌美，俺答奪之。

translations.literal: Bahannaji again betrothed the daughter of Ao'er Dusi, who was Altan Khan's granddaughter by an external daughter; she was beautiful, and Altan Khan seized her for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bahannaji then betrothed the daughter of Ao'er Dusi—Altan Khan's own granddaughter, and a great beauty—only for Altan Khan to take her for himself.

sentences.zh: 把漢恚，遂率其屬阿力哥等十人來降。

translations.literal: Bahannaji was enraged and thereupon led his followers Alige and nine others, ten men in all, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Bahannaji led ten followers, including Alige, to defect to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 大同巡撫方逢時受之，以告總督王崇古。

translations.literal: Datong Grand Coordinator Fang Fengshi received them and reported to Governor-General Wang Chonggu.
translations.idiomatic: Datong Grand Coordinator Fang Fengshi accepted the defectors and reported to Governor-General Wang Chonggu.

sentences.zh: 崇古上言：「把漢來歸，非擁眾內附者比，宜給官爵，豐館餼，飭輿馬，以示俺答。

translations.literal: Chonggu memorialized: "Bahannaji's coming to submit is not to be compared with those who defect inward while leading masses; rank and titles should be granted, lodging and rations made generous, and carriages and horses provided, to show Altan Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu memorialized: "Bahannaji's surrender is not the usual case of a tribal leader arriving with a host. We should grant him office and rank, lodge and feed him generously, and provide horses and transport—all to send a message to Altan Khan.

sentences.zh: 俺答急，則使縛送板升諸叛人；

translations.literal: If Altan Khan grows anxious, then have him bind and send the Banjin rebels;
translations.idiomatic: If Altan Khan grows alarmed, demand that he hand over the Banjin defectors bound and under guard;

sentences.zh: 不聽，即脅誅把漢牽沮之；

translations.literal: if he does not obey, then threaten to execute Bahannaji to check and frustrate him;
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses, threaten Bahannaji's life to deter him;

sentences.zh: 又不然，因而撫納，如漢置屬國居烏桓故事，使招其故部，徙近塞。

translations.literal: if that too fails, then by the same token comfort and accept him, as in the Han precedent of establishing dependent states and settling the Wuhuan, causing him to summon his old followers and move them near the passes.
translations.idiomatic: and if none of that works, settle him in comfort—after the Han model of dependent states among the Wuhuan—so he can rally his old followers and resettle them near the frontier;

sentences.zh: 俺答老且死，黃台吉立，則令把漢還，以其眾與台吉抗，我按兵助之。」

translations.literal: When Altan Khan grows old and dies and Huang Taiji rises, then send Bahannaji back so that with his followers he may resist Taiji, while we hold our troops and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan grows old and dies and Huang Taiji succeeds him, send Bahannaji back so his followers can check Huang Taiji while we hold our army in reserve to back him.

sentences.zh: 詔可，授把漢指揮使，阿力哥正千戶。

translations.literal: The edict approved; Bahannaji was appointed Assistant Commander, and Alige Chief Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved. Bahannaji was made an assistant commander, and Alige a chief company commander.

sentences.zh: 俺答方西掠吐番，聞之亟引還，約諸部入犯，崇古檄諸道嚴兵御之。

translations.literal: Altan Khan was just then raiding west among the Tibetans; hearing of it he hastily withdrew, summoned the tribes to invade together, and Chonggu issued orders to all routes to ready troops strictly in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan was raiding Tibet when he heard the news and rushed back, mustering the tribes for a joint invasion; Chonggu ordered every frontier command to mobilize in defense.

sentences.zh: 敵使來請命，崇古遣譯者鮑崇德往，言朝廷待把漢甚厚，第能縛板升諸叛人趙全等，旦送至，把漢即夕返矣。

translations.literal: An enemy envoy came to request orders; Chonggu sent interpreter Bao Chongde, saying the court had treated Bahannaji very generously and that if he could only bind the Banjin rebels Zhao Quan and others and deliver them by morning, Bahannaji would return that very evening.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy came to negotiate; Chonggu sent the interpreter Bao Chongde with word that the court had treated Bahannaji with great honor, and that if Altan Khan delivered Zhao Quan and the other Banjin rebels bound by morning, Bahannaji would return that same night.

sentences.zh: 俺答大喜，屏人語曰：「我不為亂，亂由全等。

translations.literal: Altan Khan was greatly pleased; dismissing others he said: "It is not I who make disorder—disorder comes from Quan and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan was delighted. Sending everyone else away, he said: "I do not make trouble—Zhao Quan and his crowd do.

sentences.zh: 若天子幸封我為王，長北方諸部，孰敢為患？

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven would graciously enfeoff me as king to govern the northern tribes, who would dare make trouble?
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor would grant me a princely title and leave me to govern the northern tribes, who would dare make trouble?

sentences.zh: 即死，吾孫當襲封，彼衣食中國，忍倍德乎？」

translations.literal: Even if I die, my grandson shall inherit the enfeoffment; having fed and clothed himself from China, how could he bear to betray its grace?
translations.idiomatic: Even after I die, my grandson will inherit the title—and having eaten China's bounty, how could he betray that kindness?

sentences.zh: 乃益發使與崇德來乞封，且請輸馬，與中國鐵鍋、布帛互市，隨執趙全、李自馨等數人來獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent more envoys with Chongde to beg enfeoffment, and also asked to offer horses in mutual trade with China for iron pots, cloth, and silk, thereupon seizing Zhao Quan, Li Zixin, and several others and presenting them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent more envoys with Chongde to sue for enfeoffment, offered horses in exchange for Chinese iron pots, cloth, and silk, and handed over Zhao Quan, Li Zixin, and several others.

sentences.zh: 崇古乃以帝命遣把漢歸，把漢猶戀戀，感泣再拜去。

translations.literal: Chonggu then sent Bahannaji back by the emperor's command; Bahannaji still lingered with attachment, wept in gratitude, bowed twice, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Chonggu sent Bahannaji home; the young prince lingered, wept in gratitude, bowed twice, and only then left.

sentences.zh: 俺答得孫大喜，上表謝。

translations.literal: Altan Khan, having recovered his grandson, was greatly pleased and submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed to have his grandson back, Altan Khan sent a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 崇古因上言：「朝廷若允俺答封貢，諸邊有數年之安，可乘時修備。

translations.literal: Chonggu thereupon memorialized: "If the court permits Altan Khan's enfeoffment and tribute, the frontiers will enjoy several years of peace, and we may take the opportunity to improve defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu memorialized again: "If the court grants Altan Khan enfeoffment and tribute, the frontiers may know several years of peace—time enough to rebuild our defenses.

sentences.zh: 設敵背盟，吾以數年蓄養之財力，從事戰守，愈於終歲奔命，自救不暇者矣。」

translations.literal: If the enemy break the covenant, we can apply the wealth and strength accumulated over several years to warfare and defense—better than rushing all year with no leisure even to save ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: If they break faith, we can fight from the treasury and strength we will have stored up—far better than spending year after year in frantic self-defense.

sentences.zh: 復條八事以請。

translations.literal: He again listed eight items to request.
translations.idiomatic: He appended an eight-point program to his request.

sentences.zh: 一，議封號官爵。

translations.literal: First, discuss titles, enfeoffments, and official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: First: settle titles, enfeoffments, and official ranks.

sentences.zh: 諸部行輩，俺答為尊，宜錫以王號，給印信。

translations.literal: Among the tribes by seniority Altan Khan is foremost; he should be granted a princely title and given a seal.
translations.idiomatic: By tribal seniority Altan Khan stands first among them; he should receive a princely title and an official seal.

sentences.zh: 其大枝如老把都、黃台吉及吉囊長子吉能等，俱宜授以都督。

translations.literal: The major branches such as La Bato, Huang Taiji, and Jinang's eldest son Jining should all be granted regional commander ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Major branches—La Bato, Huang Taiji, and Jinang's eldest son Jining among them—should all be made regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 弟侄子孫如兀慎打兒漢等四十六枝，授以指揮。

translations.literal: Younger brothers, nephews, and grandsons such as the forty-six branches including Ushen Da'erhan should receive assistant commander appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers, nephews, and grandsons—forty-six branches in all, including Ushen Da'erhan—should receive assistant commander appointments.

sentences.zh: 其俺答諸婿十餘枝，授以千戶。

translations.literal: Altan Khan's dozen or so branches of sons-in-law should receive company command appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan's dozen-odd branches of sons-in-law should receive company command appointments.

sentences.zh: 一，定貢額。

translations.literal: Second, fix tribute quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Second: fix tribute quotas.

sentences.zh: 每歲一入貢，俺答馬十匹，使十人。

translations.literal: Once yearly tribute mission: Altan Khan ten horses, ten envoys.
translations.idiomatic: One tribute mission each year: Altan Khan ten horses and ten envoys.

sentences.zh: 老把都、吉能、黃台吉八匹，使四人。

translations.literal: La Bato, Jining, and Huang Taiji eight horses each, four envoys each.
translations.idiomatic: La Bato, Jining, and Huang Taiji eight horses apiece and four envoys apiece.

sentences.zh: 諸部長各以部落大小為差，大者四匹，小者二匹，使各二人。

translations.literal: Each tribal leader according to tribe size: large four horses, small two horses, two envoys each.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribal leader, graded by the size of his following, should send four horses for a large tribe or two for a small one, with two envoys in either case.

sentences.zh: 通計歲貢馬不得過五百匹，使不得過百五十人。

translations.literal: In total annual tribute horses must not exceed five hundred; envoys must not exceed one hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In all, annual tribute horses must not exceed five hundred, nor envoys one hundred fifty.

sentences.zh: 馬分三等，上駟三十進御，余給價有差，老瘠者不入。

translations.literal: Horses divided in three grades; thirty top teams presented to the throne, the rest paid for at graded prices; old and emaciated not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Horses should be graded in three tiers; the thirty finest teams go to the throne, the rest are purchased at graded prices, and old or emaciated animals are rejected.

sentences.zh: 其使，歲許六十人進京，余待境上。

translations.literal: Of the envoys, sixty permitted yearly to enter the capital; the rest wait at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Of the envoys, sixty may enter the capital each year; the rest remain at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 使還，聽以馬價市繒布諸物。

translations.literal: When envoys return, they may use horse prices to buy silk, cloth, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, envoys may use the horse payments to buy silk, cloth, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 給酬賞，其賞額視三衛及西蕃諸國。

translations.literal: Rewards given; reward amounts as for the Three Guards and Western Tibetan states.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards should be paid on the same scale as for the Three Guards and the western Tibetan states.

sentences.zh: 一，議貢期、貢道。

translations.literal: Third, discuss tribute schedule and route.
translations.idiomatic: Third: settle the tribute schedule and route.

sentences.zh: 以春月及萬壽聖節四方來同之會，使人，馬匹及表文自大同左衛驗入，給犒賞。

translations.literal: On spring months and the grand assembly when all quarters come for the Longevity Festival, envoys, horses, and memorials enter through inspection at Datong Left Guard, with rewards given.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and at the grand assembly for the emperor's birthday, envoys, horses, and memorials should enter through inspection at Datong Left Guard, with rewards issued on arrival.

sentences.zh: 駐邊者，分送各城撫鎮驗賞。

translations.literal: Those staying at the frontier are sent separately to each city for inspection and reward by grand coordinators and garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Those remaining at the frontier should be sent to the appropriate cities for inspection and reward by the local coordinators and garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 入京者，押送自居庸關入。

translations.literal: Those entering the capital are escorted in through Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Those bound for the capital should be escorted in through Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 一，立互市。

translations.literal: Fourth, establish mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: establish horse markets.

sentences.zh: 其規如弘治初，北部三貢例。

translations.literal: The regulations as at the beginning of Hongzhi, following the precedent of the northern Three Tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: The rules should follow the early Hongzhi precedent for the northern Three Tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 蕃以金、銀、牛馬、皮張、馬尾等物，商販以緞紬、布匹、釜鍋等物。

translations.literal: The tribes with gold, silver, cattle, horses, pelts, horsetails and the like; merchants with satin, cloth, cauldrons, iron pots and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes would bring gold, silver, cattle, horses, pelts, horsetails, and the like; merchants would offer satin, cloth, cauldrons, iron pots, and the like.

sentences.zh: 開市日，來者以三百人駐邊外，宣府應於萬全右衛、張家口邊外，山西應於水泉營邊外。

translations.literal: On market days, arrivals of up to three hundred men camp outside the frontier; Xuanfu at Wanquan Right Guard and Zhangjiakou outside the frontier; Shanxi at Shuiquanying outside the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On market days up to three hundred men may camp outside the frontier: at Wanquan Right Guard and Zhangjiakou for Xuanfu, and at Shuiquanying for Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 一，議撫賞。

translations.literal: Fifth, discuss pacification rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: settle pacification rewards.

sentences.zh: 守市兵人布二匹，部長緞二匹、紬二匹。

translations.literal: Market guards two bolts of cloth each; tribal leaders two bolts of satin and two bolts of thin silk each.
translations.idiomatic: Market guards should receive two bolts of cloth each; tribal leaders two bolts of satin and two of thin silk.

sentences.zh: 以好至邊者，酌來使大小，量加賞犒。

translations.literal: For those who come peacefully to the frontier, considering envoy rank high or low, add rewards and gifts accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: For envoys who arrive in good faith, rewards and gifts should be added according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 一，議歸降。

translations.literal: Sixth, discuss surrender and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: settle policy on defectors.

sentences.zh: 通貢後，降者不分有罪無罪，免收納。

translations.literal: After tribute relations are established, submitters regardless of guilt or innocence are received without levy or refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Once tribute relations are established, defectors are to be accepted whether guilty or innocent, without being turned away.

sentences.zh: 其華人被擄歸正者，查別無竊盜，乃許入。

translations.literal: Chinese persons captured and returning to allegiance, if investigation shows no theft, only then permitted entry.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese captives returning to allegiance may enter only after investigation shows they committed no theft while among the enemy.

sentences.zh: 一，審經權。

translations.literal: Seventh, weigh permanent principle against temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: distinguish enduring principle from temporary expedient.

sentences.zh: 一，戒狡飾。

translations.literal: Eighth, guard against cunning evasions and pretense.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: guard against cunning evasions and false pretenses.

sentences.zh: 疏入，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; it was sent down for discussion among court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and referred to the court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 帝終從崇古言，詔封俺答為順義王，賜紅蟒衣一襲；

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed Chonggu's advice and decreed enfeoffment of Altan Khan as Prince of Shunyi, bestowing one set of red python robes;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at last accepted Chonggu's advice and enfeoffed Altan Khan as Prince of Shunyi, granting him a set of red python robes;

sentences.zh: 昆都力哈、黃台吉授都督同知，各賜紅獅子衣一襲、彩幣四表裡；

translations.literal: Kundulun and Huang Taiji were granted Vice Regional Commander, each given one set of red lion robes and four lengths of colored silk, inner and outer;
translations.idiomatic: Kundulun and Huang Taiji were made vice regional commanders, each receiving a set of red lion robes and four lengths of colored silk, lining and cover;

sentences.zh: 賓兔台吉等十人，授指揮同知；

translations.literal: Bintu Taiji and ten others were granted Vice Assistant Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Bintu Taiji and ten others were made vice assistant commanders;

sentences.zh: 那木兒台吉等十九人，授指揮僉事；

translations.literal: Namur Taiji and nineteen others were granted Assistant Commander-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Namur Taiji and nineteen others were made assistant commanders-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 打兒漢台吉等十八人，授正千戶；

translations.literal: Da'erhan Taiji and eighteen others were granted Chief Company Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Da'erhan Taiji and eighteen others were made chief company commanders;

sentences.zh: 阿拜台吉等十二人，授副千戶；

translations.literal: Abai Taiji and twelve others were granted Deputy Company Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Abai Taiji and twelve others were made deputy company commanders;

sentences.zh: 恰台吉等二人，授百戶。

translations.literal: Qia Taiji and two others were granted Platoon Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qia Taiji and two others were made platoon commanders.

sentences.zh: 昆都力哈，即老把都也。

translations.literal: Kundulun is La Bato.
translations.idiomatic: Kundulun was La Bato.

sentences.zh: 兵部采崇古議，定市令。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War adopted Chonggu's proposals and fixed market regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War adopted Chonggu's plan and issued market regulations.

sentences.zh: 秋市成，凡得馬五百餘匹，賜俺答等彩幣有差。

translations.literal: The autumn market concluded; in all more than five hundred horses were obtained, and Altan Khan and others were granted colored silk in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn market opened; more than five hundred horses were acquired in all, and Altan Khan and the others received graded gifts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 西部吉能及其侄切盡等亦請市，詔予市紅山墩暨清水營。

translations.literal: Jining of the western tribes and his nephew Qiejin also requested markets; an edict granted markets at Hongshandun and Qingshuiying.
translations.idiomatic: Jining of the western tribes and his nephew Qiejin also asked for markets; an edict granted them at Hongshandun and Qingshuiying.

sentences.zh: 市成，亦封吉能為都督同知。

translations.literal: When the market concluded, Jining was also enfeoffed as Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the market opened, Jining was also enfeoffed as vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 已而俺答請金字經及剌麻僧，詔給之。

translations.literal: Before long Altan Khan requested a gold-letter sutra and lamas; an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Altan Khan asked for a gold-letter sutra and lamas; the throne granted both.

sentences.zh: 崇古復請玉印，詔予鍍金銀印。

translations.literal: Chonggu again requested a jade seal; an edict granted a gold- and silver-plated seal.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu asked again for a jade seal; the throne granted a gold- and silver-plated seal instead.

sentences.zh: 俺答老佞佛，復請於海南建寺，詔賜寺額仰華。

translations.literal: Altan Khan in his old age doted on Buddhism and again asked to build a temple south of the frontier; an edict granted the temple name Yanghua.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age Altan Khan turned fervently to Buddhism and asked to build a temple south of the frontier; the throne granted it the name Yanghua.

sentences.zh: 俺答常遠處青山，二子，曰賓兔，居松山，直蘭州之北，曰丙兔，居西海，直河州之西，並求互市，多桀驁。

translations.literal: Altan Khan often stayed far off at Qingshan; of two sons, one called Bintu dwelt at Songshan, directly north of Lanzhou, and one called Bingtu dwelt at the Western Sea, directly west of Hezhou; both sought mutual markets and were mostly arrogant and unruly.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan often kept to distant Qingshan. He had two sons: Bintu, who lived at Songshan directly north of Lanzhou, and Bingtu, who lived at the Western Sea directly west of Hezhou. Both pressed for horse markets and were often arrogant and unruly.

sentences.zh: 俺答諭之，亦漸馴。

translations.literal: Altan Khan admonished them and they gradually grew tame.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan rebuked them, and they gradually grew more tractable.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，成梁率游擊秦得倚等擊敵於東昌堡，斬部長九人，余級八百八十四，總督梁夢龍以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli, Chengliang led Brigadier Qin Deyi and others to strike the enemy at Dongchang Fort, beheading nine tribal leaders and eight hundred eighty-four other heads; Governor-General Liang Menglong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year six, Chengliang led Brigadier Qin Deyi and others against the enemy at Dongchang Fort, beheading nine tribal leaders and eight hundred eighty-four others; Governor-General Liang Menglong reported the victory.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，祭告郊廟，御皇極門宣捷。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, offered sacrifices to inform the suburban altars and ancestral temple, and announced the victory at the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, offered sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, and announced the victory at the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，土蠻四萬騎入錦川營。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, Tümen entered Jinchuan Camp with forty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, winter, Tümen entered Jinchuan Camp with forty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 夢龍、成梁及總兵戚繼光等已預受大學士張居正方略，併力備御，敵始退。

translations.literal: Menglong, Chengliang, and Commander-in-Chief Qi Jiguang and others had already received in advance Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's strategic plan; combining strength in defense, the enemy only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Menglong, Chengliang, and Commander Qi Jiguang had already received Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's battle plan in advance; fighting together in prepared defense, they forced the enemy to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 自是敵數入，成梁等數敗之，輒斬其巨魁，又時襲擊於塞外，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: From this time the enemy entered repeatedly; Chengliang and others defeated them repeatedly, often beheading their great chiefs, and also from time to time raided beyond the passes, taking many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the raiders came again and again; Chengliang and his colleagues defeated them repeatedly, often beheading their great chiefs, and also struck beyond the passes from time to time with heavy losses inflicted on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵畏之，少戢，成梁遂以功封寧遠伯。

translations.literal: The enemy feared them and somewhat restrained themselves; Chengliang thereupon was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyuan for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders feared them and pulled back somewhat; for his merit Chengliang was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 俺答既就市，事朝廷甚謹。

translations.literal: Once Altan Khan had entered the markets, he served the court with great scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Once Altan Khan had entered the horse markets, he dealt with the court with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 部下卒有掠奪邊氓者，必罰治之，且稽首謝罪，朝廷亦厚加賞賚。

translations.literal: When his subordinates raided border commoners, he always punished them and also kowtowed in apology; the court also richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When his men looted border villagers, he punished them and kowtowed in apology to the court; the court, in turn, richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 十年春，俺答死，帝特賜祭七壇、綵緞十二表裡、布百匹，示優恤。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Altan Khan died; the emperor specially granted seven sacrificial altars, twelve lengths of colored silk inner and outer, and one hundred bolts of cloth, showing exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, spring, Altan Khan died; the emperor granted seven altars of sacrifice, twelve lengths of colored silk, lining and cover, and one hundred bolts of cloth as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 其妻哈屯率子黃台吉等，上表進馬謝，復賜幣布有差。

translations.literal: His wife Khatun led her son Huang Taiji and others in submitting a memorial and presenting horses in thanks; colored silk and cloth were again granted in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Khatun led her son Huang Taiji and the others in submitting a memorial and presenting horses in thanks; the court again granted graded gifts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 封黃台吉為順義王，改名乞慶哈。

translations.literal: Huang Taiji was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunyi and renamed Qiqingha.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunyi and given the name Qiqingha.

sentences.zh: 立三歲而死，朝廷給恤典如例。

translations.literal: Three years after his establishment he died; the court granted condolence rites according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after his succession he died; the court granted the usual condolence honors.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，子撦力克嗣。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year his son Chelik succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, spring, his son Chelik succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其妻三娘子，故俺答所奪之外孫女而為婦者也，歷配三王，主兵柄，為中國守邊保塞，眾畏服之，乃敕封為忠順夫人，自宣大至甘肅不用兵者二十年。

translations.literal: His wife Third Lady was formerly the granddaughter Altan Khan had seized and taken as wife; successively married to three kings, she held military authority, guarded the frontier and passes for China, and all feared and submitted to her; she was thereupon enfeoffed by edict as Lady of Zhongshun, and from Xuan-Datong to Gansu no troops were used for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Third Lady, was the granddaughter Altan Khan had seized and taken for himself; married in turn to three khans, she held real military power, guarded the frontier for China, and was feared and obeyed by all. The throne enfeoffed her as Lady of Zhongshun, and for twenty years no armies were needed from Xuan-Datong to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 及撦力克西行遠邊，而套部莊禿賴等據水塘，卜失兔、火落赤等據莽剌、捏工兩川，數犯甘、涼、洮、氓、西寧間。

translations.literal: When Chelik moved west to the distant frontier, the Ordos tribes Zhuang Tulai and others held Shuitang, Bushitu and Huoluo Chi and others held the two valleys of Mangla and Nie'gong, and repeatedly raided between Ganzhou, Liangzhou, Taozhou, Minzhou, and Xining.
translations.idiomatic: When Chelik moved west to the distant frontier, the Ordos leader Zhuang Tulai and others seized Shuitang, while Bushitu, Huoluo Chi, and others held the Mangla and Nie'gong valleys, repeatedly raiding the country between Ganzhou, Liangzhou, Taozhou, Minzhou, and Xining.

sentences.zh: 他部落亡慮數十種，出沒塞下，順逆不常。

translations.literal: Other tribes, no doubt several tens of kinds, appeared and vanished below the passes, obedient or rebellious without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of other tribes, at least, lurked below the passes, raiding or submitting by turns with no fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，十九年詔並停撦力克市賞。

translations.literal: The emperor hated this; in the nineteenth year an edict stopped Chelik's markets and rewards altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was disgusted; in the nineteenth year an edict cut off Chelik's horse markets and frontier rewards altogether.

sentences.zh: 已而撦力克叩邊輸服，率眾東歸，獨莊禿賴、卜失兔等寇抄如故。

translations.literal: Before long Chelik knocked at the border and submitted in defeat, leading his multitude east to return; only Zhuang Tulai, Bushitu, and others raided and plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chelik came to the frontier to surrender, led his people back east, and only Zhuang Tulai, Bushitu, and the like continued to raid as before.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，別部明安、土昧分犯榆林邊，總兵杜桐御之，斬獲五百人，殺明安。

translations.literal: That winter, of another division Ming'an and Tumei separately invaded the Yulin frontier; Regional Commander Du Tong resisted them, beheaded and captured five hundred men, and killed Ming'an.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Ming'an and Tumei of a separate division attacked the Yulin frontier on separate fronts. Regional Commander Du Tong met them in battle, killed and captured five hundred men, and slew Ming'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，寧夏叛將哱拜等勾卜失兔、莊禿賴等，大舉入寇，總兵李如松擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Ningxia rebel generals Baba and others colluded with Bushitu, Zhuang Tulai, and others and launched a great invasion; Regional Commander Li Rusong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, the Ningxia rebel generals Baba and others joined with Bushitu, Zhuang Tulai, and others for a major raid. Regional Commander Li Rusong routed them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，延綏巡撫李春光奏：「套部納款已久，自明安被戮而寇恨深，西夏黨逆而貢市絕，延鎮連年多事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Yansui Grand Coordinator Li Chunguang memorialized: "The Ordos tribes have submitted allegiance for a long time; since Ming'an was slain their raiding hatred is deep, the Western Xia faction has rebelled and tribute markets have ceased, and Yan town has had many successive years of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Yansui Grand Coordinator Li Chunguang memorialized: "The Ordos tribes submitted long ago, but since Ming'an was killed their bitterness for raiding runs deep. With the Western Xia faction in rebellion and tribute markets cut off, the Yan region has been embroiled year after year.

sentences.zh: 今東西各部皆乞款，而卜失兔挾私叵測，邊長兵寡，制御為難。

translations.literal: Now the eastern and western tribes all beg to submit, yet Bushitu harbors private designs hard to fathom; the frontier is long and soldiers few, and control is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Now the eastern and western tribes are all asking to submit, but Bushitu's private motives are impossible to read. The frontier is long, our troops are few, and keeping control is hard.

sentences.zh: 宜察敵情，審時勢。

translations.literal: One should observe enemy conditions and examine the circumstances of the time.
translations.idiomatic: We should read the enemy's intentions and weigh the circumstances of the moment.

sentences.zh: 敵入犯則血戰，偶或小失，應寬吏議。

translations.literal: When the enemy invades, then fight to the blood; if occasionally there is a small setback, officials' deliberations should be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy invades, fight without holding back; if commanders suffer a minor setback now and then, their cases should be judged leniently.

sentences.zh: 倘敵真心效順，相機議撫，不可忘戰備也。」

translations.literal: If the enemy truly and sincerely submits, take opportunity to discuss pacification, but one must not forget war preparedness."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy is genuinely willing to submit, we may entertain pacification when the moment is right—but we must never neglect war readiness."

sentences.zh: 帝命兵部傳飭各邊。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Ministry of War to transmit instructions to all frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of War to relay these instructions to every frontier command.

sentences.zh: 秋，卜失兔入固原，游擊史見戰死。

translations.literal: In autumn Bushitu entered Guyuan; Mobile Corps Commander Shi Jian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Bushitu entered Guyuan. Mobile Corps Commander Shi Jian was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 延綏總兵麻貴御之，閱月始退。

translations.literal: Yansui Regional Commander Ma Gui resisted him; only after a full month did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yansui Regional Commander Ma Gui met him in battle, and Bushitu did not withdraw until a month had passed.

sentences.zh: 全陝震動。

translations.literal: All Shaanxi was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shaanxi was shaken.

sentences.zh: 其年，東部炒花犯鎮武堡，總兵董一元與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: That year the eastern tribe Chao Hua invaded Zhenwu Fort; Regional Commander Dong Yiyuan fought him and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: That year the eastern chieftain Chao Hua attacked Zhenwu Fort. Regional Commander Dong Yiyuan met him in battle and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 明年春，松部宰僧等犯陝西，總督葉夢熊督卻之。

translations.literal: The next spring, Zaiseng and others of the Song tribe invaded Shaanxi; Governor-general Ye Mengxiong supervised their repulse.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Zaiseng and others of the Song division raided Shaanxi. Governor-general Ye Mengxiong directed the defense and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 秋，海部永邵卜犯西寧，總督三邊李旼檄參將達雲、游擊白澤暨馬其撒、卜爾加諸屬番，設伏邀擊，大敗之，斬六百八十三級。

translations.literal: In autumn, Yong Shaobu of the Hai tribe invaded Xining; Three Frontiers Governor-general Li Min dispatched orders to Assistant Regional Commander Da Yun, Mobile Corps Commander Bai Ze, together with Maqisa, Bu'erjia, and various dependent tribes, who set an ambush to intercept and strike, utterly defeated them, and beheaded six hundred eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yong Shaobu of the Hai tribe raided Xining. Three Frontiers Governor-general Li Min ordered Assistant Regional Commander Da Yun, Mobile Corps Commander Bai Ze, and the dependent tribes Maqisa, Bu'erjia, and others to lay an ambush. They crushed the raiders and took six hundred eighty-three heads.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝大悅，且以屬番效命，追敘前總制鄭雒功，賞賚並及雒。

translations.literal: When word of the victory arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased; moreover, because the dependent tribes had shown loyal service, he posthumously recorded the merits of the former overall commander Zheng Luo and extended rewards and gifts to Luo as well.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory reached court, the emperor was delighted. Because the dependent tribes had fought loyally, he also credited the former frontier commander Zheng Luo retroactively and extended rewards to Luo himself.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，總督李釐以勁兵分三道出塞，襲卜失兔營，共斬四百九級，獲馬畜器械數千。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, Governor-general Li Li took elite troops divided into three routes beyond the passes, raided Bushitu's camp, beheaded four hundred nine in all, and captured several thousand horses, livestock, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, spring, Governor-general Li Li led crack troops out in three columns beyond the passes, struck Bushitu's camp, took four hundred nine heads, and seized thousands of horses, livestock, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 火落赤部眾復窺伺洮州，釐遣參將周國柱等擊之於莽剌川腦，斬一百三十六級。

translations.literal: The multitude of Huoluo Chi's tribe again spied and watched Taozhou; Li sent Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Guozhu and others to strike them at Mangla Chuan Nao and beheaded one hundred thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo Chi's followers again prowled around Taozhou. Li dispatched Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Guozhu and others to strike them at the headwaters of the Mangla River and took one hundred thirty-six heads.

sentences.zh: 秋，著力兔、阿赤兔、火落赤等合謀犯西邊，炒花亦擁眾犯廣寧，守將皆嚴兵卻之。

translations.literal: In autumn Zhuli Tu, Achitu, Huoluo Chi, and others combined in conspiracy to invade the western frontier; Chao Hua also led a multitude to invade Guangning; the defending generals all marshaled strict troops and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhuli Tu, Achitu, Huoluo Chi, and others joined forces to raid the west, while Chao Hua also led a large host against Guangning. The frontier garrisons met them with full force and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 二十五年秋，海部寇甘鎮，官軍擊走之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-fifth year the Hai tribe raided Gan town; government troops struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, autumn, the Hai tribes raided the Gansu frontier. Government troops beat them back.

sentences.zh: 冬，炒花糾土蠻諸部寇遼東，殺掠無算。

translations.literal: In winter Chao Hua rallied the Tuman tribes and others to raid Liaodong; killing and plundering were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chao Hua rallied the Tuman tribes and others to raid Liaodong, killing and plundering without measure.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，復寇遼東，總兵李如松遠出搗巢，死之。

translations.literal: The next summer he again raided Liaodong; Regional Commander Li Rusong marched far out to smash their nests and died in the attempt.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer they raided Liaodong again. Regional Commander Li Rusong led a deep strike against their camps and was killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，釐等分道出襲火落赤等於松山，走之，復其地。

translations.literal: In winter Li and others went out on separate routes to raid Huoluo Chi and others at Songshan, put them to flight, and recovered the territory.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Li and others attacked Huoluo Chi and his allies at Songshan in separate columns, drove them off, and recovered the ground.

sentences.zh: 二十七年詔復撦力克市賞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year an edict restored Chelik's markets and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year an edict restored Chelik's horse markets and frontier rewards.

sentences.zh: 時釐等築松山，諸部紛叛，延、寧守臣共擊之，殺獲甲首幾三千。

translations.literal: At this time Li and others built Songshan; the tribes turned rebellious one after another; the defending officials of Yan and Ning jointly struck them and killed and captured nearly three thousand armored chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li and others were fortifying Songshan. The tribes broke into revolt one after another; the garrison commanders of Yan and Ning joined forces and killed or captured nearly three thousand armored leaders.

sentences.zh: 明年，著力兔、宰僧、莊禿賴等乞通款，不許。

translations.literal: The next year Zhuli Tu, Zaiseng, Zhuang Tulai, and others begged to open submission, but were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhuli Tu, Zaiseng, Zhuang Tulai, and others asked to submit, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 邊臣王見賓等復為請，詔復套部貢市。

translations.literal: Frontier officials Wang Jianbin and others again pleaded on their behalf; an edict restored the Ordos tribes' tribute markets.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials Wang Jianbin and others petitioned again on their behalf, and an edict restored tribute markets for the Ordos tribes.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，海部數入陝西塞，兵備副使李自實，總兵蕭如薰、達雲等擊走之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the Hai tribe repeatedly entered the Shaanxi passes; Military Preparation Vice Commissioner Li Zishi, Regional Commanders Xiao Ruxun, Da Yun, and others struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year the Hai tribes repeatedly breached the Shaanxi frontier. Military Preparation Vice Commissioner Li Zishi and Regional Commanders Xiao Ruxun and Da Yun drove them back.

sentences.zh: 三十三年夏，東部宰賽誘殺慶雲堡守禦熊鑰，詔革其市賞。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-third year the eastern tribe Zaisai treacherously killed Qingyun Fort Defensive Commander Xiong Yao; an edict abolished their markets and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, summer, the eastern chieftain Zaisai lured and killed Qingyun Fort defensive commander Xiong Yao. An edict cut off his horse markets and rewards.

sentences.zh: 三十五年夏，總督徐三畏言：「河套之部與河東之部不同。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-fifth year Governor-general Xu Sanwei said: "The tribes of the Ordos loop and the tribes east of the river are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, summer, Governor-general Xu Sanwei wrote: "The Ordos tribes and the tribes east of the river are not alike.

sentences.zh: 東部事統於一，約誓定，歷三十年不變。

translations.literal: Eastern affairs are unified under one head; covenants are fixed and have not changed for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tribes answer to a single authority; their covenants were fixed decades ago and have held for thirty years without change.

sentences.zh: 套部分四十二枝，各相雄長，卜失兔徒建空名於上。

translations.literal: The Ordos tribes divide into forty-two branches, each vying as overlord; Bushitu merely holds an empty title above them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos split into forty-two branches, each lord fighting the others for supremacy. Bushitu holds little more than an empty title over them.

sentences.zh: 西則火落赤最狡，要挾最無厭；

translations.literal: In the west Huoluo Chi is most cunning; his demands and coercion are most insatiable;
translations.idiomatic: In the west Huoluo Chi is the most cunning, his demands and extortion the most insatiable;

sentences.zh: 中則擺言太以父明安之死，無歲不犯；

translations.literal: In the center Bai Yantai, because of his father Ming'an's death, raids every year without fail;
translations.idiomatic: In the center Bai Yantai, nursing his father's death at Ming'an's hands, raids without fail year after year;

sentences.zh: 東則沙計爭為監市，與炒花朋逞。

translations.literal: In the east Shaji contends to serve as market overseer and runs riot together with Chao Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the east Shaji vies to control the tribute markets and runs wild alongside Chao Hua.

sentences.zh: 西陲搶攘非一日矣。

translations.literal: Strife and turmoil on the western frontier have not been a matter of a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier has been in turmoil for years.

sentences.zh: 然眾雖號十萬，分為四十二枝，多者不過二三千騎，少者一二千騎耳。

translations.literal: Yet though their multitude is said to reach one hundred thousand, divided into forty-two branches the larger have no more than two or three thousand horsemen, the smaller only one or two thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though they claim a hundred thousand men, split into forty-two branches the largest bands field no more than two or three thousand riders, and the smallest only one or two thousand.

sentences.zh: 宜分其勢，納其款，俾先順者獲賞，後至者拒剿。

translations.literal: One should divide their power, accept their submission, let those who submit first receive rewards, and those who come later be repulsed and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: We should divide their strength, accept their submissions, reward those who come first, and fight those who hold back.

sentences.zh: 仍須主戰以張國威。」

translations.literal: Still one must uphold battle as the main policy to display national majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Even so, we must keep fighting readiness at the center of policy to uphold the empire's prestige."

sentences.zh: 時已許宰賽及火落赤諸部復貢市矣。

translations.literal: At that time permission had already been granted for Zaisai and the tribes of Huoluo Chi and others to resume tribute markets.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already allowed Zaisai, Huoluo Chi, and their allies to reopen tribute markets.

sentences.zh: 未幾撦力剋死，未有嗣，忠順夫人率所部仍效貢職。

translations.literal: Before long Chelik died without an heir; Lady of Zhongshun led her tribes and still performed tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chelik died without an heir. Lady of Zhongshun continued to lead her followers in paying tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 西部銀定、歹青數擁眾犯東西邊。

translations.literal: In the west Yinding and Daiqing repeatedly led multitudes to invade the eastern and western frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the west Yinding and Daiqing repeatedly led their followers in raids on both the eastern and western frontiers.

sentences.zh: 延綏部猛克什力亦以挾賞故，常沿邊抄掠。

translations.literal: Mengkeshili of the Yansui tribe also, because of holding rewards hostage, constantly raided and plundered along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Mengkeshili of the Yansui division also raided constantly along the frontier, using tribute demands as leverage.

sentences.zh: 卜失兔欲婚於忠順，忠順拒之。

translations.literal: Bushitu wished to marry into the Zhongshun house; Zhongshun refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu sought a marriage alliance with Lady of Zhongshun; she refused.

sentences.zh: 其所部素囊台吉、五路台吉等，各不相下，封號久未定。

translations.literal: The Sudai Taiji, Wulu Taiji, and others of his tribes each would not submit to the other; enfeoffment titles had long gone unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Sudai Taiji, Wulu Taiji, and other subordinate chiefs refused to yield to one another, and their court titles had long remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，卜失兔始婚於忠順，東、西諸部長皆具狀為請封。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Bushitu at last married into the Zhongshun house; chiefs of the eastern and western tribes all filed petitions requesting enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year Bushitu finally married into Lady of Zhongshun's house. Chiefs from the eastern and western tribes all petitioned the court to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 忠順夫人旋卒，詔封卜失兔為順義王，而以把漢比吉素效恭順，封忠義夫人。

translations.literal: Lady of Zhongshun soon died; an edict enfeoffed Bushitu as Prince of Shunyi, and because Bahannibi had long shown respectful submission, enfeoffed her as Lady of Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Zhongshun soon died. An edict enfeoffed Bushitu as Prince of Shunyi and, because Bahannibi had long served loyally, enfeoffed her as Lady of Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 卜失兔為撦力克孫，襲封時，已少衰，所制止山、大二鎮外十二部。

translations.literal: Bushitu was Chelik's grandson; at the time he inherited enfeoffment he had already declined somewhat; what he controlled was only the twelve tribes outside the Shan and Da garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu was Chelik's grandson. By the time he inherited his title his power had already waned; he controlled only the twelve tribes beyond the Shan and Da garrisons.

sentences.zh: 其部長五路、素囊及兀慎台吉等，兵力皆與順義埒。

translations.literal: The tribal chiefs Wulu, Sudai, and Wushen Taiji and others all had military strength equal to the Prince of Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate chiefs such as Wulu, Sudai, and Wushen Taiji commanded forces equal to the Prince of Shunyi's own.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因宣大總督涂宗浚言，各予升賞如例。

translations.literal: The court, following Xuan-Datong Governor-general Tu Zongjun's memorial, granted each promotions and rewards according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Xuan-Datong Governor-general Tu Zongjun, the court granted each the usual promotions and rewards.

sentences.zh: 其年，炒花糾虎墩兔三犯遼東。

translations.literal: That year Chao Hua rallied Hudun Tu to thrice invade Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chao Hua joined with Hudun Tu to raid Liaodong three times.

sentences.zh: 虎墩兔者，居插漢兒地，亦曰插漢兒王子，元裔也。

translations.literal: Hudun Tu was one who dwelt in Chahar territory, also called the Chahar prince, a descendant of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hudun Tu lived in Chahar lands and was also known as the Chahar prince—a descendant of the Yuan house.

sentences.zh: 其祖打來孫始駐牧宣塞外，俺答方強，懼為所並，乃徙帳於遼，收福余雜部，數入掠薊西，四傳至虎墩兔，遂益盛。

translations.literal: His ancestor Dalai Sun first pastured troops outside the Xuan passes; Altan Khan was then strong and he feared being swallowed by him, so he moved his encampment to Liaodong, gathered the Fuyu mixed tribes, repeatedly entered to plunder west of Ji, and through four generations down to Hudun Tu his power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Dalai Sun first grazed his herds outside the Xuan frontier. Altan Khan was then at the height of his power, and fearing annexation he moved his tents to Liaodong, gathered the Fuyu and other mixed tribes, and repeatedly raided west of Ji. Four generations later Hudun Tu had grown stronger still.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，炒花復合宰賽、暖兔以三萬騎入掠，至平虜、大寧。

translations.literal: The next summer Chao Hua again combined with Zaisai and Nuan Tu with thirty thousand horsemen to enter and plunder, reaching Pinglu and Daning.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer Chao Hua joined Zaisai and Nuan Tu in a raid thirty thousand strong, pushing as far as Pinglu and Daning.

sentences.zh: 既求撫賞，許之。

translations.literal: Having then sought pacification rewards, they were granted.
translations.idiomatic: They then sought pacification payments—and got them.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，猛克什力寇懷遠及保寧。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Mengkeshili raided Huaiyuan and Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year Mengkeshili raided Huaiyuan and Baoning.

sentences.zh: 延綏總兵官秉忠等破之。

translations.literal: Yansui Regional Commander Guan Bingzhong and others defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yansui Regional Commander Guan Bingzhong and others routed him.

sentences.zh: 斬二百二十一級。

translations.literal: Two hundred twenty-one were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred twenty-one heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 明年，插部數犯遼東。

translations.literal: The next year the Chahar tribe repeatedly invaded Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Chahar division raided Liaodong repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 已，掠義州，攻陷大安堡，兵民死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Before long they plundered Yizhou, captured and overthrew Da'an Fort, and soldiers and civilians who died were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they sacked Yizhou, overran Da'an Fort, and killed a great many soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，總兵杜文煥數破套部猛克什力等於延綏邊，火落赤、擺言太及吉能、切盡、歹青、沙計東西諸部皆懼，先後來請貢市。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Regional Commander Du Wenhuan repeatedly defeated Mengkeshili and others of the Ordos tribes on the Yansui frontier; Huoluo Chi, Bai Yantai, and Jining, Qiejin, Daiqing, Shaji, and the eastern and western tribes all grew fearful and came one after another to request tribute markets.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year Regional Commander Du Wenhuan repeatedly defeated Mengkeshili and other Ordos leaders on the Yansui frontier. Huoluo Chi, Bai Yantai, Jining, Qiejin, Daiqing, Shaji, and chiefs from east and west alike grew afraid and petitioned one after another to reopen tribute markets.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，我大清兵起，略撫順及開原，插部乘隙擁眾挾賞。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year our Great Qing army rose; it overran Fushun and Kaiyuan; the Chahar tribe seized the opening to lead a multitude and hold rewards hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year the armies of our Great Qing rose up, overrunning Fushun and Kaiyuan. The Chahar tribe seized the moment to gather a host and demand frontier payments.

sentences.zh: 西部阿暈妻滿旦亦以萬騎自石塘路入掠薊鎮白馬關及高家、馮家諸堡。

translations.literal: In the west Ayun's wife Mandan also with ten thousand horsemen entered from the Shitang route to plunder Baima Pass of Ji town and the forts of Gaojia, Fengjia, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the west Ayun's wife Mandan also led ten thousand riders through the Shitang road to raid Baima Pass in the Ji region and the forts of Gaojia, Fengjia, and others.

sentences.zh: 游擊硃萬良御之，被圍。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Zhu Wanliang resisted them and was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Zhu Wanliang met them in battle and was surrounded.

sentences.zh: 羽書日數十至，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Urgent dispatches arrived by the dozens each day; court and country were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches arrived by the dozen each day, and the court and provinces went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 頃之，滿旦亦叩關乞通貢。

translations.literal: Before long Mandan also knocked at the pass begging to open tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mandan also came to the passes seeking to reopen tribute relations.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，大清兵滅宰賽及北關金台什、布羊古等。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year the Great Qing army destroyed Zaisai and the northern pass chiefs Jintai Shi, Buyanggu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year Qing forces destroyed Zaisai and the northern pass chiefs Jintai Shi, Buyanggu, and others.

sentences.zh: 金台什孫女為虎墩兔婦，於是薊遼總督文球、巡撫周永春等以利啖之，俾聯結炒花諸部，以捍大清兵，給白金四千。

translations.literal: Jintai Shi's granddaughter was Hudun Tu's wife; thereupon Ji-Liao Governor-general Wen Qiu, Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun, and others tempted him with profit, had him link Chao Hua's tribes and others to resist the Great Qing army, and gave four thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Jintai Shi's granddaughter was married to Hudun Tu. Ji-Liao Governor-general Wen Qiu, Grand Coordinator Zhou Yongchun, and others therefore bought him off, had him join with Chao Hua and other tribes to resist the Qing armies, and paid him four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 明年，為泰昌元年，加賞至四萬。

translations.literal: The next year, which was the first year of Taichang, additional rewards were raised to forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The following year—the first year of the Taichang reign—additional payments were raised to forty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 虎乃揚言助中國，邀索無厭。

translations.literal: Hudun Tu then proclaimed that he would aid China, demanding and seeking without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Hudun Tu then declared he would aid China—and his demands knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年秋，吉能犯延綏邊，榆林總兵杜文煥擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Tianqi Jining invaded the Yansui frontier; Yulin Regional Commander Du Wenhuan defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi, autumn, Jining raided the Yansui frontier. Yulin Regional Commander Du Wenhuan routed him.

sentences.zh: 明年春，復大掠延安黃花峪，深入六百里，殺掠居民數萬。

translations.literal: The next spring he again greatly plundered Huanghuayu of Yan'an, penetrating six hundred li deep, killing and plundering several tens of thousands of residents.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he launched a major raid on Huanghuayu in Yan'an, penetrating six hundred li deep and killing or carrying off tens of thousands of civilians.

sentences.zh: 三年春，銀定糾眾再掠西邊，官軍擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Yinding rallied a multitude to again plunder the western frontier; government troops defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, spring, Yinding rallied his followers for another raid on the western frontier. Government troops defeated him.

sentences.zh: 明年春，復謀入故巢，犯松山，為守臣馮任等所敗。

translations.literal: The next spring he again plotted to enter his old nest, invaded Songshan, and was defeated by the defending officials Feng Ren and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he tried to return to his old base and attacked Songshan, but frontier commander Feng Ren and others defeated him.

sentences.zh: 夏，遂糾海西古六台吉等犯甘肅，總兵董繼舒擊之，斬三百餘級。

translations.literal: In summer he then rallied Haixi Guliu Taiji and others to invade Gansu; Regional Commander Dong Jishu struck them and beheaded more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he joined Haixi chieftain Guliu Taiji and others in a raid on Gansu. Regional Commander Dong Jishu met them in battle and took more than three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 其年，歹青以領賞嘩於邊，邊人格殺之。

translations.literal: That year Daiqing raised an uproar at the frontier over receiving rewards, and frontier people killed him in retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: That year Daiqing caused a riot at the frontier over his reward payment, and local border troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 歹青，虎墩兔近屬也，邊臣議歲給償命銀一萬三千有奇，而虎怏怏，益思飏去。

translations.literal: Daiqing was a close kinsman of Hudun Tu; frontier officials deliberated giving compensation for his life of slightly more than thirteen thousand taels of silver per year, but Hudun Tu was resentful and all the more inclined to flee away.
translations.idiomatic: Daiqing was a close kinsman of Hudun Tu. Frontier officials proposed paying slightly more than thirteen thousand taels a year in blood-money compensation, but Hudun Tu was aggrieved and more inclined than ever to break away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大清兵襲破炒花，所部皆散亡，半歸於插漢。

translations.literal: Before long the Great Qing army raided and broke Chao Hua; his tribes all scattered and perished, half returning to Chahar.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qing forces struck and shattered Chao Hua. His followers scattered, and half of them went over to Chahar.

sentences.zh: 時卜失兔益衰，號令不行於諸部，部長干兒罵等歲數犯延綏諸邊。

translations.literal: At this time Bushitu declined ever further; his commands did not prevail among the tribes; tribal chiefs Gan'erma and others year after year repeatedly invaded the various Yansui frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: By then Bushitu's power had waned further still; his orders no longer carried among the tribes, and chiefs such as Gan'erma raided the Yansui frontier year after year.

sentences.zh: 七慶台吉及敖目比吉、毛乞炭比吉等，亦各擁眾往來窺伺塞下。

translations.literal: Qiqing Taiji and Aomu Biji, Maoqitan Biji, and others also each led multitudes back and forth to spy and watch below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqing Taiji, Aomu Biji, Maoqitan Biji, and others also led their bands back and forth, prowling below the passes.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，虎墩兔攻哈喇嗔及白言台吉、卜失兔諸部，皆破之，遂乘勝入犯宣大塞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen Hudun Tu attacked Haracina and Baitai Taiji, Bushitu's tribes, and broke them all; then taking advantage of victory he entered to invade the Xuan-Datong passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen Hudun Tu attacked Haracina, Baitai Taiji, Bushitu, and their allies, defeating them all. He then pressed his advantage and breached the Xuan-Datong frontier.

sentences.zh: 秋，帝御平台，召總督王象乾，詢以方略，象乾對言：「御插之道，宜令其自相攻。

translations.literal: In autumn the emperor attended at the terrace platform, summoned Governor-general Wang Xiangqian, and asked him for strategy; Xiangqian replied: "The way to defend against the Chahar is to have them attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor held court on the terrace platform, summoned Governor-general Wang Xiangqian, and asked his strategy. Xiangqian answered: "The way to counter the Chahar is to set them against one another.

sentences.zh: 今卜失兔西走套內，白台吉挺身免，而哈喇嗔所部多被擄，不足用。

translations.literal: Now Bushitu has fled west into the Ordos interior, Baitai Taiji alone escaped with his body, and most of Haracina's tribes have been captured—not enough to be useful.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu has already fled west into the Ordos. Baitai Taiji alone escaped with his life, while most of Haracina's followers have been captured and are of little use.

sentences.zh: 永邵卜最強，約三十萬人，合卜失兔所部並聯絡朵顏三十六家及哈喇嗔餘眾，可以御插漢。

translations.literal: Yong Shaobu is strongest, about three hundred thousand men; combining Bushitu's tribes and also linking the thirty-six clans of Doyan and Haracina's remaining multitude, he can resist Chahar.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shaobu is the strongest, with some three hundred thousand men. Together with Bushitu's followers, the thirty-six Doyan clans, and Haracina's remaining bands, he could hold Chahar in check.

sentences.zh: 然與其構之，水如撫而用之。」

translations.literal: Yet rather than set them against one another, it would be better to pacify and employ them."
translations.idiomatic: But rather than pit them against each other, it would be better to pacify them and put them to use."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「插漢意不受撫，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Chahar plainly will not accept pacification—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Chahar clearly has no mind to accept pacification. What then?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當從容籠絡。」

translations.literal: He replied: "One must calmly win them over and bind them."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "We must win them over patiently."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如不款何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If they do not submit, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "And if they refuse to submit?"

sentences.zh: 象乾復密奏，帝善之，命往與督師袁崇煥共計。

translations.literal: Xiangqian again memorialized in secret; the emperor approved and ordered him to go and consult jointly with supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqian submitted a secret memorial. The emperor approved and ordered him to go discuss the matter jointly with supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan.

sentences.zh: 象乾至邊，與崇煥議合，皆言西靖而東自寧，虎不款，而東西並急，因定歲予插金八萬一千兩，以示羈縻。

translations.literal: When Xiangqian reached the frontier he agreed in counsel with Chonghuan; both said that if the west were settled the east would calm itself; if Hudun Tu did not submit, both east and west would be urgent together; they therefore fixed an annual grant to the Chahar of eighty-one thousand taels of silver to show restraint and control.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangqian reached the frontier he and Chonghuan agreed on a plan: secure the west and the east would settle of its own accord; if Hudun Tu refused to submit, both fronts would be strained at once. They therefore settled on paying the Chahar eighty-one thousand taels of silver annually as a tethering payment.

sentences.zh: 大同巡撫張宗衡上言：「插來宣大，駐新城，去大同僅二百里，三閱月未敢近前，飢餓窮乏，插與我等耳。

translations.literal: Datong Grand Coordinator Zhang Zongheng memorialized: "The Chahar came to Xuan-Datong and encamped at New Town, only two hundred li from Datong; three months passed and they dared not draw near; hunger, poverty, and exhaustion—the Chahar and we are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Datong Grand Coordinator Zhang Zongheng wrote: "The Chahar have come to Xuan-Datong and camp at New Town, barely two hundred li from Datong. Three months have passed and they still dare not advance. Starving and destitute, they are no better off than we are.

sentences.zh: 插恃撫金為命，兩年不得，資用已竭，食盡馬乏，暴骨成莽。

translations.literal: The Chahar rely on pacification silver as their life; for two years they have not received it; supplies are exhausted, food is gone and horses spent, exposed bones form wild thickets.
translations.idiomatic: The Chahar live on pacification payments. They have gone two years without receiving them; their supplies are gone, their food exhausted and horses spent, and bleached bones litter the wild.

sentences.zh: 插之望款不啻望歲，而我遺之金繒、牛羊、茶果、米谷無算，是我適中其欲也。

translations.literal: The Chahar's hope for submission is no less than hope for harvest; yet we send them silks, cattle and sheep, tea, fruit, and grain beyond counting—we are only fitting their desires exactly.
translations.idiomatic: The Chahar long for submission no less than farmers long for harvest—and we shower them with silks, cattle, sheep, tea, fruit, and grain without measure. We are giving them exactly what they want.

sentences.zh: 插炰烋悖慢，耳目不忍睹聞，方急款尚如是。

translations.literal: The Chahar are arrogant, fierce, and insolent; eyes and ears cannot bear to see or hear; even while urgently seeking submission they are still like this.
translations.idiomatic: The Chahar are arrogant and insolent beyond what eyes can watch or ears can hear—and even while begging to submit they behave like this.

sentences.zh: 使插士馬豐飽，其憑陵狂逞，可勝道哉。」

translations.literal: If the Chahar's soldiers and horses were full and fed, their leaning on force and wild rampaging—can it all be told?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Chahar's warriors and horses were well fed, how wild their depredations would be—words can scarcely describe it."

sentences.zh: 象乾言：「款局垂成而復棼之，既示插以不信，亦非所以為國謀。」

translations.literal: Xiangqian said: "The submission settlement was nearly complete and to unravel it again both shows the Chahar that we are untrustworthy and is not the way to plan for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqian argued: "The submission talks were nearly settled—to unravel them now would show the Chahar we cannot be trusted, and it is no way to serve the state."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝是象乾議，詔宗衡毋得異同。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor sided with Xiangqian's view and ordered Zongheng not to raise objections.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, the emperor sided with Xiangqian and ordered Zongheng not to dissent.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，虎復擁眾至延綏紅水灘，乞增賞未遂，即縱掠塞外，總兵吳自勉御卻之。

translations.literal: The next autumn Hudun Tu again led a multitude to Yansui's Hongshui Beach, begged for increased rewards without success, and at once let loose raiding outside the passes; Regional Commander Wu Zimian resisted and repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Hudun Tu gathered a host at Hongshui Beach in Yansui, demanded additional payments without success, and immediately turned to raiding beyond the passes. Regional Commander Wu Zimian drove him back.

sentences.zh: 既而東附大清兵攻龍門。

translations.literal: Before long he turned east and attached himself to the Great Qing army to attack Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went over to the Qing and joined their attack on Longmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為大清兵所擊。

translations.literal: Before long he was struck by the Great Qing army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was defeated by Qing forces.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，插漢聞大清兵至，盡驅部眾渡河遠遁。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, hearing that Great Qing troops had arrived, the Chahar drove all their followers across the river and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year, hearing that Qing armies were coming, the Chahar drove all their people across the river and fled.

sentences.zh: 是時，韃靼諸部先後歸附於大清。

translations.literal: At this time the Tartar tribes in succession submitted to the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Tartar tribes were submitting to the Qing one after another.

sentences.zh: 明年，大清兵遂大會諸部於兀蘇河南岡，頒軍律焉。

translations.literal: The next year Qing troops then assembled the tribes on the south bank of the Usun River and promulgated military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Qing army assembled the tribes on the south bank of the Usun River and issued military regulations.

sentences.zh: 而虎已卒，乃追至上都城，盡俘插漢妻孥部眾。

translations.literal: Ligdan had already died; they then pursued to Shangdu and wholly captured the Chahar women, children, and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Ligdan was already dead; the Qing pursued to Shangdu and took all the Chahar women, children, and followers captive.

sentences.zh: 其後，套部歲入寧夏、甘、涼境，巡撫陳奇瑜、總兵馬世龍、督師洪承疇等輒擊敗之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Ordos tribes yearly entered the territories of Ningxia, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou; Grand Coordinator Chen Qiyu, Regional Commander Ma Shilong, Supreme Commander Hong Chengchou, and others repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Ordos tribes raided Ningxia, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou yearly; Chen Qiyu, Ma Shilong, Hong Chengchou, and others repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 套部乾兒罵，亦為總兵尤世祿所斬。

translations.literal: The Ordos leader Gendenma was also beheaded by Regional Commander You Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos leader Gendenma was also killed by Regional Commander You Shilu.

sentences.zh: 迄明世，邊陲無寧，致中原盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty the frontier knew no peace, leading bandits to swarm in the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming the frontier never knew peace, and banditry swarmed across the central plains.

sentences.zh: 當事者狃與俺答等貢市之便，見插之恣於東也，謂歲捐金錢數十萬，冀苟安旦夕，且覬收之為用，而卒不得。

translations.literal: Those in charge clung to the convenience of tribute markets with Altan and others; seeing the Chahar rampant in the east, they thought to donate several hundred thousand in gold and cash yearly, hoping for a night’s respite and also coveting to win them for use—yet in the end they could not.
translations.idiomatic: Officials clung to the ease of tribute markets with Altan and others; seeing the Chahar run riot in the east, they paid out hundreds of thousands yearly hoping for a night’s peace and dreaming of turning them to Ming use—but never could.

sentences.zh: 迨其後也，明未亡而插先斃，諸部皆折入於大清。

translations.literal: In the sequel, before the Ming perished the Chahar first were destroyed; all the tribes bent into the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, before the Ming fell the Chahar were destroyed first and all the tribes submitted to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 國計愈困，邊事愈棘，朝議愈紛，明亦遂不可為矣。

translations.literal: State finances grew ever more strained, frontier affairs ever more thorny, court debate ever more confused—and the Ming thus became beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: State finances grew strained, frontier affairs desperate, and court debate chaotic—and the Ming became beyond saving.

sentences.zh: 韃靼地，東至兀良哈，西至瓦剌。

translations.literal: Tartar territory extended east to the Uriyangqad and west to the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: Tartar lands stretched east to the Uriyangqad and west to the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 當洪、永、宣世，國家全盛，頗受戎索，然畔服亦靡常。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu, Yongle, and Xuande reigns the state was at its height and largely held the nomads in rein, yet rebellion and submission were never constant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu, Yongle, and Xuande reigns the empire was at its height and largely held the nomads in check, yet loyalty and rebellion never held steady.

sentences.zh: 正統後，邊備廢弛，聲靈不振。

translations.literal: After Zhengtong frontier defenses were neglected and imperial prestige did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengtong frontier defenses collapsed and imperial prestige waned.

sentences.zh: 諸部長多以雄傑之姿，恃其暴強，迭出與中夏抗。

translations.literal: Tribal chiefs mostly with heroic stature relied on their violent strength and came forth in turn to contend with the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs, often men of heroic stature, relied on brute force and rose in turn to challenge the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 邊境之禍，遂與明終始雲。

translations.literal: Frontier calamity thus ran from the Ming’s beginning to its end.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier disaster thus ran from the Ming’s beginning to its end.
